at kalde.explanation: "At kalde" means "to call", as in naming or shouting for someone: Vi kalder hunden Max (We call the dog Max). Han kalder på mig (He calls out to me). For phoning, say at ringe: Jeg ringer til dig (I will call you).

sentence.da: Vi vil **kalde** vores baby Emma.
sentence.en: We want to call our baby Emma.

at kalde på.explanation: "At kalde på" means "to call for", to call out so someone comes: Jeg kalder på tjeneren (I call for the waiter). Without på, at kalde means to name: Vi kalder hunden Max (We call the dog Max).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **kalde på** tjeneren, når vi skal betale.
sentence.en: I will call for the waiter when we want to pay.

at kaste.explanation: "At kaste" means "to throw": Han kastede bolden til mig (He threw the ball to me). With op, it means "to throw up": Jeg skal kaste op (I am going to throw up).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **kaste** sten i vandet.
sentence.en: The children want to throw stones into the water.

at kaste håndklædet i ringen.explanation: "At kaste håndklædet i ringen" means "to throw in the towel", to give up. It comes from boxing, where a trainer throws a towel into the ring to stop a fight. Danes use it for anything, such as a project or a diet.

forms.da: Vi vil ikke kaste håndklædet i ringen

sentence.da: Efter tre nederlag vil han **kaste håndklædet i ringen**.
sentence.en: After three defeats, he wants to throw in the towel.

at kaste op.explanation: "At kaste op" means "to throw up", as in being sick. It is made of kaste (to throw) and op (up), and without op, kaste is just to throw: Jeg kaster bolden (I throw the ball).

sentence.da: Han er syg og vil **kaste op**.
sentence.en: He is sick and wants to throw up.

at kategorisere.explanation: "At kategorisere" means "to categorize", to put things into types by what they share: Vi kategoriserer dyr efter størrelse (We categorize animals by size).

sentence.da: Biblioteket vil **kategorisere** bøgerne efter emne.
sentence.en: The library wants to categorize the books by topic.

at kede sig.explanation: "At kede sig" means "to be bored": Jeg keder mig (I am bored). The little word changes with the person: Han keder sig (He is bored), Vi keder os (We are bored).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **kede sig**, når de ikke har legetøj.
sentence.en: The children can get bored when they have no toys.

at kende.explanation: "At kende" means "to know (a person or place)", or to be familiar with something: Jeg kender Anna (I know Anna). To know a fact, use at vide (to know), as in Jeg ved, at hun bor her (I know that she lives here).

forms.en: I have known (a person or place)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **kende** dine venner bedre.
sentence.en: I would like to know your friends better.

at kidnappe.explanation: "At kidnappe" means "to kidnap", to take a person away by force and hold them. It looks like the English word.

sentence.da: De vil **kidnappe** hende og kræve penge.
sentence.en: They want to kidnap her and demand money.

at kigge.explanation: "At kigge" means "to look": Kig her! (Look here!). It is often followed by på (at): Jeg kigger på billedet (I am looking at the picture). In a store, you may hear Jeg kigger bare (I'm just looking).

sentence.da: Jeg vil bare **kigge** på tøjet i butikken.
sentence.en: I just want to look at the clothes in the store.

at kigge efter.explanation: "At kigge efter" means "to look for": Jeg kigger efter mine briller (I am looking for my glasses). It can also mean "to keep an eye on": Kig efter børnene (Keep an eye on the kids).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **kigge efter** mine nøgler i bilen.
sentence.en: I have to look for my keys in the car.

at kildre.explanation: "At kildre" means "to tickle", to touch someone lightly so that they squirm or laugh: Han kildrede mig på foden (He tickled me on the foot). It also names the feeling itself: Det kildrer (It tickles).

sentence.da: Han griner, når jeg vil **kildre** ham.
sentence.en: He laughs when I want to tickle him.

at klage.explanation: "At klage" means "to complain", and what you complain about comes after over (about): Han klager over støjen (He is complaining about the noise). The person you complain to comes after til (to): Jeg klager til banken (I am complaining to the bank).

related.en: a formal complaint about a product

sentence.da: Jeg vil **klage** over den kolde mad.
sentence.en: I will complain about the cold food.

at klappe.explanation: "At klappe" means "to clap" and "to pat". You clap your hands to show you liked a show, and you pat a pet with a gentle touch: Jeg klapper hunden (I pat the dog).

sentence.da: Alle vil **klappe**, når sangeren er færdig.
sentence.en: Everyone will clap when the singer is done.

at klare.explanation: "At klare" means "to manage" or "to cope with" something: Han klarer opgaven (He manages the task). It also means "to pass": Jeg klarede prøven (I passed the test).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt **klare** den opgave alene.
sentence.en: I can handle that task on my own.

at klare op.explanation: "At klare op" means "to clear up", for weather that gets better: Det klarer op i aften (It will clear up this evening). For tidying a room, use at rydde op (to tidy up) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg håber, det vil **klare op** i morgen.
sentence.en: I hope it will clear up tomorrow.

at klare sig.explanation: "At klare sig" means "to get by", and also "to do well": Hun klarer sig fint i Danmark (She is doing fine in Denmark). Jeg klarer mig uden bil (I get by without a car).

forms.en: I have gotten by / done well

sentence.da: Hun er voksen og kan **klare sig** selv.
sentence.en: She is grown up and can take care of herself.

at klassificere.explanation: "At klassificere" means "to classify", to place something in a fixed system, as scientists do with animals and plants: Forskerne klassificerer et nyt dyr (The scientists are classifying a new animal).

sentence.da: Forskerne vil **klassificere** planterne efter deres blade.
sentence.en: The scientists want to classify the plants by their leaves.

at klatre.explanation: "At klatre" means "to climb" with your hands and feet: Børnene klatrer i et træ (The children climb a tree). It also works for prices going up: Priserne klatrer (Prices are climbing).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **klatre** op i det høje træ.
sentence.en: I want to climb up the tall tree.

at klemme.explanation: "At klemme" means "to squeeze" or "to pinch", for example a lemon or your finger in a door: Jeg klemte fingeren i døren (I pinched my finger in the door).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **klemme** en citron over fisken.
sentence.en: I want to squeeze a lemon over the fish.

at klikke.explanation: "At klikke" means "to click", with a mouse or on a screen. You click on something with på: Jeg klikker på linket (I click on the link).

sentence.da: Du skal **klikke** på den blå knap.
sentence.en: You have to click on the blue button.

at klippe.explanation: "At klippe" means "to cut (with scissors)": Jeg klipper papir (I cut paper). It is also the word for hair: Hun klipper mit hår (She cuts my hair).

sentence.da: Hun vil **klippe** mit hår i morgen.
sentence.en: She will cut my hair tomorrow.

at klynge sig.explanation: "At klynge sig" means "to cling": to grip something tightly, often out of fear or need. It is followed by til (to): klynge sig til rækværket (cling to the railing), klynge sig til håbet (cling to hope).

sentence.da: Barnet vil **klynge sig** til sin mor, når det er bange.
sentence.en: The child will cling to its mother when it is scared.

at klæde.explanation: "At klæde" means "to suit": clothes, colors or a haircut that make a person look nice. The clothes come first and the person after: Blåt klæder hende (Blue suits her).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, at den røde kjole vil **klæde** dig.
sentence.en: I think the red dress will suit you.

at klæde sig af.explanation: "At klæde sig af" means "to get undressed". The small word after klæde changes with the person: Jeg klæder mig af (I get undressed), Hun klæder sig af (She gets undressed). The opposite is at klæde sig på (to get dressed).

sentence.da: Barnet skal **klæde sig af** og tage et bad.
sentence.en: The child has to get undressed and take a bath.

at klæde sig på.explanation: "At klæde sig på" means "to get dressed". The small word sig (oneself) changes with the person: du klæder dig på (you get dressed), han klæder sig på (he gets dressed). To put on one item, say at tage en jakke på (to put on a jacket).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **klæde sig på** nu.
sentence.en: The children have to get dressed now.

at klø.explanation: "At klø" means "to itch", and also "to scratch" something to ease it. Danes say Det klør (It itches). To scratch yourself, add sig: at klø sig (to scratch oneself).

sentence.da: Huden kan **klø**, når en myg har stukket dig.
sentence.en: Your skin can itch when a mosquito has bitten you.

at klø sig.explanation: "At klø sig" means "to scratch oneself", to scratch your own skin where it itches. Sig (oneself) is needed. Where you scratch comes after på (on): Jeg klør mig på ryggen (I scratch my back).

sentence.da: Hunden vil **klø sig** bag øret med poten.
sentence.en: The dog wants to scratch itself behind the ear with its paw.

at knappe.explanation: "At knappe" means "to button", to fasten clothes with buttons: knappe skjorten (button the shirt). Add op to open them again: at knappe op (to unbutton).

sentence.da: Du skal **knappe** frakken, fordi det er koldt.
sentence.en: You must button the coat because it is cold.

at knibe.explanation: "At knibe" means "to pinch": to take a bit of skin between two fingers, as in Hun kneb mig i armen (She pinched my arm). With øjnene sammen it means to squint: knibe øjnene sammen (squint). Det kniber med pengene (Money is tight) is a set phrase for having hardly enough.

sentence.da: Man må **knibe** øjnene sammen, når solen skinner kraftigt.
sentence.en: You have to squint when the sun shines strongly.

at knuse.explanation: "At knuse" means "to crush" and "to smash": Han knuste glasset (He smashed the glass). It is also used for feelings: Det knuste hendes hjerte (It broke her heart).

sentence.da: Hun vil **knuse** nødderne med en hammer.
sentence.en: She wants to crush the nuts with a hammer.

at knytte.explanation: "At knytte" means "to tie" in a knot, and also "to connect". It is used in set phrases: knytte næven (clench your fist) and knytte et venskab (form a friendship). For shoelaces, use at binde (to tie).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **knytte** rebet fast, fordi båden driver væk.
sentence.en: I must tie the rope fast because the boat is drifting away.

at knække.explanation: "At knække" means "to crack" or "to break" something hard by bending or hitting it: knække en pind (break a stick). For a broken bone, Danes use at brække (to break): Jeg har brækket armen (I have broken my arm).

sentence.da: Man skal **knække** skallen for at spise nødden.
sentence.en: To eat the nut, you must crack the shell.

at knæle.explanation: "At knæle" means "to kneel", to go down on your knees, for example to pray or to propose. It is built on et knæ (a knee): Hun knæler ved sengen (She kneels by the bed).

sentence.da: Man kan **knæle**, så begge knæ rører gulvet.
sentence.en: You can kneel so that both knees touch the floor.

at koge.explanation: "At koge" means "to boil", or to cook in boiling water, for example eggs, pasta and potatoes: Vandet koger (The water is boiling). For cooking food in general, use at lave mad (to cook): Jeg laver mad (I am cooking).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **koge** kartofler i vand.
sentence.en: I am going to boil potatoes in water.

at koge over.explanation: "At koge over" means "to boil over", when a liquid gets too hot and runs out of the pot: Vandet koger over (The water boils over). It also works for feelings: Hun koger over af vrede (She is boiling over with anger).

sentence.da: Mælken kan **koge over**, når du ikke passer på.
sentence.en: The milk can boil over when you are not watching.

at kollidere.explanation: "At kollidere" means "to collide", to run into each other with force, such as cars, boats or planes. It is also used for plans or interests that clash. After it, use med (with): Bilen kolliderede med en cykel (The car collided with a bicycle).

sentence.da: To biler kan **kollidere**, når vejen er glat.
sentence.en: Two cars can collide when the road is slippery.

at kombinere.explanation: "At kombinere" means "to combine", to put two things together: Hun kombinerer rødt og blåt (She combines red and blue).

sentence.da: Du kan **kombinere** ris og grøntsager.
sentence.en: You can combine rice and vegetables.

at komme.explanation: "At komme" means "to come", for arriving and for being on the way: Jeg kommer nu (I am coming now). Hvor kommer du fra? means "Where are you from?". It is also used for what will happen next: Det kommer til at regne (It is going to rain).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme** til din fest i morgen.
sentence.en: I will come to your party tomorrow.

at komme an på.explanation: "At komme an på" means "to depend on": Det kommer an på vejret (It depends on the weather). On its own, it is a common answer: Kommer du? Det kommer an på (Are you coming? It depends).

sentence.da: Det vil **komme an på** vejret i morgen.
sentence.en: It will depend on the weather tomorrow.

at komme for sent.explanation: "At komme for sent" means "to be late", literally to arrive too late: Jeg kom for sent til skolen (I was late for school). For a train or bus, say forsinket (delayed): Toget er forsinket (The train is delayed).

forms.en: I have been late / arrived late

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **komme for sent** til mødet.
sentence.en: I do not want to be late for the meeting.

at komme forbi.explanation: "At komme forbi" means "to come by", to stop in for a visit: Kom forbi i aften (Come by tonight). It can also mean "to get past": Vi kan ikke komme forbi bilen (We cannot get past the car).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **komme forbi** i morgen.
sentence.en: You are welcome to come by tomorrow.

at komme frem.explanation: "At komme frem" means "to arrive", often after a trip: Vi kom frem klokken seks (We arrived at six o'clock). It also means "to come forward": Han kom frem fra mængden (He came forward from the crowd).

sentence.da: Toget skal **komme frem** klokken seks.
sentence.en: The train is due to arrive at six o'clock.

at komme godt ud af det med.explanation: "At komme godt ud af det med" means "to get along with", to have a good relationship with someone: Jeg kommer godt ud af det med min chef (I get along well with my boss). Put dårligt (badly) in place of godt to say the opposite: Jeg kommer dårligt ud af det med min nabo (I get along badly with my neighbor).

forms.da: at komme godt ud af det med
jeg kommer godt ud af det med
jeg kom godt ud af det med
jeg er kommet godt ud af det med

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **komme godt ud af det med** mine nye kolleger.
sentence.en: I would like to get along well with my new colleagues.

at komme hjem.explanation: "At komme hjem" means "to come home", to arrive at home: Hvornår kommer du hjem? (When will you get home?). To say you are leaving for home, use at tage hjem (to go home): Jeg tager hjem nu (I am going home now).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme hjem** i aften.
sentence.en: I want to come home tonight.

at komme i gang.explanation: "At komme i gang" means "to get started" on work, a meeting or a project: Vi kommer i gang klokken ni (We get started at nine o'clock). Add med to say what: Jeg kom i gang med opgaven (I got started on the task).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **komme i gang** med arbejdet.
sentence.en: I would like to get started on the work.

at komme i tanke om.explanation: "At komme i tanke om" means "to remember" or "to think of" something that suddenly comes to mind: Jeg kom i tanke om nøglerne (I remembered the keys). What you think of comes after om (of).

forms.da: jeg er kommet i tanke om

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **komme i tanke om** hans navn.
sentence.en: I can't think of his name.

at komme ind.explanation: "At komme ind" means "to come in", to enter a room or building, and also "to get in" when someone has to let you: Kom ind! (Come in!). Vi kom ikke ind i klubben (We could not get into the club).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **komme ind** uden nøgle.
sentence.en: I cannot get in without a key.

at komme med.explanation: "At komme med" means "to come along", and also "to bring": Kommer du med? (Are you coming along?) Hun kom med kage (She brought cake).

sentence.da: Vil du **komme med** i biografen i aften?
sentence.en: Do you want to come along to the movies tonight?

at komme ned.explanation: "At komme ned" means "to come down", for example down the stairs or from a higher floor: Kom ned og spis! (Come down and eat!).

sentence.da: Kan du **komme ned** af trappen?
sentence.en: Can you come down the stairs?

at komme op.explanation: "At komme op" means "to come up", and also "to get up", for example from a chair or the floor. Kom op! can also mean "Come on!". To get out of bed, Danes usually say at stå op (to get up).

forms.en: I have come up / gotten up

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **komme op** af stolen.
sentence.en: I cannot get up from the chair.

at komme over.explanation: "At komme over" means "to get over" something hard: Han kom aldrig over det (He never got over it). Kom over til os! (Come over to our place!) uses it for a visit.

sentence.da: Det tager tid at **komme over** en stor sorg.
sentence.en: It takes time to get over great sorrow.

at komme sig.explanation: "At komme sig" means "to recover" from an illness, an injury or a shock: Han kommer sig hurtigt (He recovers quickly). It always keeps sig (oneself), because at komme alone means "to come".

sentence.da: Efter operationen skal han **komme sig** i to uger.
sentence.en: After the surgery, he has to recover for two weeks.

at komme til skade.explanation: "At komme til skade" means "to get hurt" by accident: Han kom til skade i går (He got hurt yesterday). Add på (on) and the body part: Jeg kom til skade på benet (I hurt my leg).

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **komme til skade** på isen.
sentence.en: The children must not get hurt on the ice.

at komme tilbage.explanation: "At komme tilbage" means "to come back" or "to return", to be somewhere again after you have left: Jeg kommer snart tilbage (I will be back soon). Tilbage (back) works with other words too: at give tilbage (to give back), at betale tilbage (to pay back).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme tilbage** til Danmark næste år.
sentence.en: I want to come back to Denmark next year.

at komme ud.explanation: "At komme ud" means "to come out" or "to get out", of a room, house or building: Kom ud! means "Come out!" and Han kommer ud af skolen means "He comes out of the school".

forms.en: I have come out / gotten out

sentence.da: Jeg vil **komme ud** af huset.
sentence.en: I want to get out of the house.

at komme videre.explanation: "At komme videre" means "to move on", to get past a problem or a place: Jeg skal komme videre (I have to move on). It can be a trip too: Vi kom videre til næste by (We went on to the next town).

sentence.da: Vi bliver ikke her, men vil **komme videre** i dag.
sentence.en: We are not staying here, but want to move on today.

at kommentere.explanation: "At kommentere" means "to comment", to give your view or response about something, such as a post, a match or the news: Hun kommenterer videoen (She is commenting on the video). Danish needs no word for on here: the thing comes right after the verb.

sentence.da: Politikeren ville ikke **kommentere** sagen til pressen.
sentence.en: The politician did not want to comment on the case to the press.

at kommunikere.explanation: "At kommunikere" means "to communicate": Vi kommunikerer på dansk (We communicate in Danish). The person you communicate with comes after med (with): Jeg kommunikerer med kunden (I communicate with the customer).

sentence.da: Vi kan **kommunikere** på engelsk og dansk.
sentence.en: We can communicate in English and Danish.

at kompensere.explanation: "At kompensere" means "to compensate", to make up for a loss or a weakness. It is often followed by for: at kompensere for en fejl (to compensate for a mistake).

sentence.da: Han vil **kompensere** for sin højde med hurtige fødder.
sentence.en: He wants to compensate for his height with fast feet.

at komplicere.explanation: "At komplicere" means "to complicate", to make something harder than it was. It often comes with tingene (things): Det komplicerer tingene (That complicates things).

sentence.da: Nye regler kan **komplicere** en opgave, der var nem før.
sentence.en: New rules can complicate a task that used to be easy.

at komponere.explanation: "At komponere" means "to compose", to create music by writing it. It is about making the piece, not playing it: Hun komponerer, og han spiller (She composes and he plays).

sentence.da: Hun vil **komponere** musik til en film.
sentence.en: She wants to compose music for a film.

at koncentrere sig.explanation: "At koncentrere sig" means "to concentrate": Jeg kan ikke koncentrere mig (I cannot concentrate). For the thing you focus on, add om (on): Vi koncentrerer os om opgaven (We are concentrating on the task).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **koncentrere sig**, når der er larm.
sentence.en: It is hard to concentrate when there is noise.

at konfirmere.explanation: "At konfirmere" means "to confirm" in a Christian ceremony where a young person, usually around fourteen, confirms their baptism. Many Danes are konfirmeret (confirmed) and have a family party afterward, often even if they are not very religious.

sentence.da: Præsten vil **konfirmere** de unge i kirken i maj.
sentence.en: The priest will confirm the young people in the church in May.

at konkludere.explanation: "At konkludere" means "to conclude", to reach a result after thinking or studying something. It is usually followed by at (that) and the result.

sentence.da: Efter testen kan vi **konkludere**, at medicinen virker.
sentence.en: After the test we can conclude that the medicine works.

at konkurrere.explanation: "At konkurrere" means "to compete", to try to win against others. You compete with someone (med, with) or for something (om, for): Vi konkurrerer om prisen (We compete for the prize).

sentence.da: Mange firmaer vil **konkurrere** om de samme kunder.
sentence.en: Many companies compete for the same customers.

at konstatere.explanation: "At konstatere" means "to state" or "to establish": to say that a fact is now clear after you have seen or checked it. Politiet konstaterede, at ingen var kommet til skade (The police established that nobody had been hurt).

sentence.da: Jeg må **konstatere**, at vi ikke har nok penge.
sentence.en: I have to state that we do not have enough money.

at konstruere.explanation: "At konstruere" means "to construct", to design and build something with a plan. It is used for things with a clear design: at konstruere en maskine (to construct a machine).

sentence.da: Ingeniøren skal **konstruere** en bro over fjorden.
sentence.en: The engineer is going to construct a bridge over the fjord.

at kontakte.explanation: "At kontakte" means "to contact", to get in touch with a person or a company. It sounds formal. With friends you would say Send mig en besked (Send me a message).

sentence.da: Du kan **kontakte** lægen på telefon.
sentence.en: You can contact the doctor by phone.

at kontrollere.explanation: "At kontrollere" means "to check", to make sure something is right. It also means "to inspect" when an official does it: Politiet kontrollerer bilerne (The police check the cars).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **kontrollere** tallene en gang til.
sentence.en: I want to check the numbers once more.

at koordinere.explanation: "At koordinere" means "to coordinate", to arrange people or tasks so they work well together. It is about fitting the parts together, not about being the boss.

sentence.da: Hun skal **koordinere** arbejdet mellem de tre hold.
sentence.en: She is going to coordinate the work between the three teams.

at kopiere.explanation: "At kopiere" means "to copy". It works for photocopying and for files on a computer.

sentence.da: Kan du **kopiere** de her papirer til mig?
sentence.en: Can you copy these papers for me?

at korrigere.explanation: "At korrigere" means "to correct", to fix mistakes in something that already exists, such as a text or a number. It does not mean to be right: for that, use at have ret (to be right).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **korrigere** vores fejl i opgaven.
sentence.en: The teacher will correct our mistakes in the assignment.

at kortlægge.explanation: "At kortlægge" means "to map", but mostly not as a drawing. It means to find out and list in detail what exists, such as a problem or the facts: kortlægge problemet (map out the problem).

sentence.da: Forskerne vil **kortlægge**, hvordan sygdommen spreder sig.
sentence.en: The researchers want to map how the disease spreads.

at koste.explanation: "At koste" means "to cost". It is mostly used with det (it) or de (they): Hvad koster det? (How much does it cost?). Because a thing does the costing, the forms above start with det (it) instead of jeg (I).

sentence.da: Den nye bluse vil **koste** hundrede kroner.
sentence.en: The new blouse will cost a hundred kroner.

at kramme.explanation: "At kramme" means "to hug", to hold someone close in your arms to show love or comfort. The word for the hug itself is et kram: Giv mig et kram! (Give me a hug!)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **kramme** min mor, fordi jeg savner hende.
sentence.en: I want to hug my mom because I miss her.

at kravle.explanation: "At kravle" means "to crawl", moving on hands and knees, like a baby. It also means to go up using your hands and feet: Han kravler op i træet (He crawls up the tree).

sentence.da: Min lille søn kan **kravle** meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: My little son can crawl very fast.

at kritisere.explanation: "At kritisere" means "to criticize" and says what you find wrong. It does not have to sound angry: Jeg kritiserer planen roligt (I criticize the plan calmly).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **kritisere** mit forslag.
sentence.en: You are welcome to criticize my suggestion.

at krybe.explanation: "At krybe" means "to creep / crawl", to move low along the ground, like a snake or a worm. The past is irregular: jeg krøb (I crept).

sentence.da: Slangen kan **krybe** ind under den store sten.
sentence.en: The snake can creep in under the big stone.

at krydre.explanation: "At krydre" means "to season", to give food more taste by adding things like pepper or chili. You say what you add with med (with): at krydre med chili (to season with chili).

sentence.da: Man skal **krydre** suppen med salt og peber.
sentence.en: You have to season the soup with salt and pepper.

at krydse.explanation: "At krydse" means "to cross", to go from one side of something to the other, such as a street, a bridge or a border.

sentence.da: Børnene skal **krydse** gaden, når lyset er grønt.
sentence.en: The children must cross the street when the light is green.

at kræve.explanation: "At kræve" means "to require" or "to demand". Used about things, it says what is needed. Used about a person, it is stronger and means insisting: Han kræver svar (He demands an answer).

sentence.da: Det nye job vil **kræve** meget tid.
sentence.en: The new job will require a lot of time.

at kunne.explanation: "At kunne" means "can / to be able to". Another action word follows straight after it, with no at in between: Jeg kan svømme (I can swim).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **kunne** svømme som en fisk.
sentence.en: I would like to be able to swim like a fish.

at kunne lide.explanation: "At kunne lide" means "to like": Jeg kan lide kaffe (I like coffee). With a person, you usually add godt (well): Jeg kan godt lide dig (I like you). To say you do not like something, add ikke (not): Jeg kan ikke lide det (I don't like it).

sentence.da: Du vil **kunne lide** maden her.
sentence.en: You will like the food here.

at kurere.explanation: "At kurere" means "to cure", to make someone healthy again. You can cure a person or an illness: at kurere en sygdom (to cure a disease).

sentence.da: Lægerne håber at kunne **kurere** hende helt.
sentence.en: The doctors hope to be able to cure her completely.

at kvaje sig.explanation: "At kvaje sig" means "to mess up": to do something clumsy or silly by accident, often small and a bit embarrassing: Jeg kvajede mig og tabte kaffen (I messed up and dropped the coffee). It is for small slips, not big failures.

sentence.da: Man kan nemt **kvaje sig**, når man er nervøs.
sentence.en: It is easy to mess up when you are nervous.

at kvalificere.explanation: "At kvalificere" means "to qualify", to make someone or something good enough for a goal. It mostly comes with sig (oneself): you qualify yourself for the next round.

sentence.da: Holdet vil **kvalificere** sig til slutspillet i år.
sentence.en: The team wants to qualify for the playoffs this year.

at kvidre.explanation: "At kvidre" means "to chirp", the high, light sounds small birds make: Fuglene kvidrer i haven (The birds chirp in the garden).

sentence.da: Om foråret kan man høre små fugle **kvidre** i træerne.
sentence.en: In spring, you can hear small birds chirp in the trees.

at kvittere.explanation: "At kvittere" means "to sign for" something handed to you, or "to acknowledge" it: kvittere for en pakke (sign for a package). It also means to answer a good deed with a sign of gratitude: kvittere for hjælpen (show gratitude for the help).

sentence.da: Jeg måtte **kvittere** for nøglen, da jeg hentede den.
sentence.en: I had to sign for the key when I picked it up.

at kvæle.explanation: "At kvæle" means "to strangle" or "to choke" someone, to stop them from breathing. It is also used for stopping things from growing: kvæle en idé (smother an idea). To choke on food, Danes say Jeg fik det galt i halsen (I got it down the wrong way).

sentence.da: Planterne vil **kvæle** hinanden, hvis de står for tæt.
sentence.en: The plants will smother each other if they stand too close.

at kysse.explanation: "At kysse" means "to kiss", touching someone with your lips to show love or care. To say where, add på (on): Han kyssede hende på kinden (He kissed her on the cheek).

sentence.da: Hun vil **kysse** sin baby godnat.
sentence.en: She wants to kiss her baby good night.

at kæle.explanation: "At kæle" means "to cuddle / pet", to show love with soft touches. It is used for people and animals, and it goes with med (with).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker at **kæle** med den lille kat.
sentence.en: The children love to cuddle with the little cat.

at kæmpe.explanation: "At kæmpe" means "to fight" in a battle or a match, and also "to struggle": Hun kæmper med lektierne (She struggles with her homework). For a quarrel, use skændes (to argue).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **kæmpe** for mit hold.
sentence.en: I will fight for my team.

at kæmpe for.explanation: "At kæmpe for" means "to fight for" something you believe in: Vi kæmper for bedre løn (We are fighting for better pay). In sports, it means trying hard to win: Holdet kæmper for sejren (The team is fighting for the win).

sentence.da: Vi må **kæmpe for** vores drømme.
sentence.en: We have to fight for our dreams.

at købe.explanation: "At købe" means "to buy". Add for and the price to say what you paid: Jeg købte den for hundrede kroner (I bought it for a hundred kroner).

sentence.da: Vi kan **købe** mælk i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: We can buy milk at the supermarket.

at købe ind.explanation: "At købe ind" means "to buy groceries", or to do your shopping, mostly for food and things for the home. At købe (to buy) is more general. You often hear Jeg skal ud og købe ind (I am going out to shop).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **købe ind** til aftensmad.
sentence.en: I need to buy groceries for dinner.

at køre.explanation: "At køre" means "to drive", or to ride in a vehicle: Jeg kører i bil (I go by car). It is also used for a bus or train that runs: Bussen kører hver time (The bus runs every hour). For a bike, you usually say at cykle (to cycle).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **køre** bilen til arbejde i morgen.
sentence.en: I want to drive the car to work tomorrow.

at køre fast.explanation: "At køre fast" means "to get stuck", first of all a car or other vehicle. It also fits a conversation or a plan: Samtalen kørte fast (The conversation got stuck).

sentence.da: Bilen kan **køre fast** i den dybe sne.
sentence.en: The car can get stuck in the deep snow.

at køre forbi.explanation: "At køre forbi" means "to drive past", for example a shop. It can also mean "to swing by", to visit briefly: Jeg kører forbi hos dig i aften (I will swing by your place tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **køre forbi** og hente dig.
sentence.en: I can swing by and pick you up.

at køre hjem.explanation: "At køre hjem" means "to drive home", and works for any vehicle that takes you there, such as a car or a bus. For going on foot, use at gå hjem (to walk home).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **køre hjem**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to drive home.

en kaffeautomat.explanation: "En kaffeautomat" means "a coffee machine" that sells cups: you put in coins or tap a card and a cup of coffee comes out. It stands in offices, stations and hospitals. For the machine you use at home to brew coffee, say en kaffemaskine (a coffee maker).

sentence.da: Jeg kan købe en kop varm kaffe fra en **kaffeautomat** for ti kroner.
sentence.en: I can buy a cup of hot coffee from a vending machine for ten kroner.

en kaffekande.explanation: "En kaffekande" means "a coffee pot", the pot that coffee is poured from at the table. It is built from kaffe (coffee) and kande (pot). A kande is any pot or jug for pouring, also en mælkekande (a milk jug).

sentence.da: Jeg hælder kaffe fra en **kaffekande** i min kop.
sentence.en: I pour coffee from a coffee pot into my cup.

en kaffekop.explanation: "En kaffekop" means "a coffee cup", the cup itself. En kop kaffe (a cup of coffee) is the coffee inside it.

sentence.da: Min **kaffekop** er tom, og jeg vil have mere.
sentence.en: My coffee cup is empty and I want more.

en kaffemaskine.explanation: "En kaffemaskine" means "a coffee maker", the appliance that brews coffee. It is built from kaffe (coffee) and maskine (machine), which also appears in en vaskemaskine (a washer).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter vand i min **kaffemaskine** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I put water in my coffee maker every morning.

en kaffepause.explanation: "En kaffepause" means "a coffee break", a short time away from work. It is built from kaffe (coffee) and pause (break). Pause also works alone: Vi holder pause (We stop for a while).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **kaffepause** og læser avisen.
sentence.en: I take a coffee break and read the paper.

en kage.explanation: "En kage" means "a cake", but Danes also use kage for pastries and other sweet baked treats.

sentence.da: Vi spiser **kage** til min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: We eat cake for my birthday.

en kagedej.explanation: "En kagedej" means "a cake batter", the raw mix of flour, eggs, butter and sugar before it is baked. It is built from en kage (a cake) and en dej (a dough).

sentence.da: Når **kagedej** er klar, skal den i ovnen i en halv time.
sentence.en: When the cake batter is ready, it goes in the oven for half an hour.

en kageform.explanation: "En kageform" means "a cake pan", the dish you bake a cake in. It is built from kage (cake) and form (mold). Form also means a shape: en kage i form af et hjerte (a cake in the shape of a heart).

sentence.da: Hun bager en chokoladekage i en **kageform**.
sentence.en: She bakes a chocolate cake in a cake pan.

en kagerulle.explanation: "En kagerulle" means "a rolling pin", the roller for flattening dough. It is built from kage (cake) and rulle (roll). Do not mix it up with en rullekage (a rolled sponge cake), which is the cake itself.

sentence.da: En **kagerulle** er lavet af træ og bruges til dej.
sentence.en: A rolling pin is made of wood and is used for dough.

en kaj.explanation: "En kaj" means "a quay" or "a dock", the stone or wooden edge of the water where boats tie up.

sentence.da: Båden lægger til ved **kaj** nummer to.
sentence.en: The boat docks at dock number two.

en kakerlak.explanation: "En kakerlak" means "a cockroach", a flat, brown animal that comes out at night and likes warm, damp places such as kitchens. It eats food scraps, so people want it gone.

sentence.da: Der løb en **kakerlak** hen over køkkengulvet i nat.
sentence.en: A cockroach ran across the kitchen floor last night.

en kalender.explanation: "En kalender" means "a calendar", which shows the whole year, on paper or in your phone, so you can plan ahead.

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mødet i min **kalender**.
sentence.en: I write the meeting in my calendar.

en kalkun.explanation: "En kalkun" means "a turkey", the bird, and without en it also means the meat: Jeg vil have kalkun på min sandwich (I want turkey on my sandwich). It is not the country: that is Tyrkiet (Turkey).

sentence.da: Vi steger en stor **kalkun** i ovnen.
sentence.en: We roast a big turkey in the oven.

en kalorie.explanation: "En kalorie" means "a calorie". You mostly hear it for more than one: Hvor mange kalorier er der i en pizza? (How many calories are in a pizza?)

sentence.da: Jeg tæller hver **kalorie** i min mad.
sentence.en: I count every calorie in my food.

en kalv.explanation: "En kalv" means "a calf", a young cow. The meat is called kalvekød (veal).

sentence.da: Koen har fået en lille **kalv**.
sentence.en: The cow has had a little calf.

en kam.explanation: "En kam" means "a comb", a flat tool with a row of teeth that you pull through your hair.

sentence.da: Hun bruger en **kam** i håret.
sentence.en: She uses a comb in her hair.

en kamel.explanation: "En kamel" means "a camel", a large desert animal that people ride and use to carry heavy loads.

sentence.da: En **kamel** kan gå længe uden vand.
sentence.en: A camel can walk for a long time without water.

en kammerat.explanation: "En kammerat" means "a buddy", someone you do things with, and also "a comrade", a person who shares your team or your cause.

sentence.da: Jeg spiller fodbold med en **kammerat** hver lørdag.
sentence.en: I play soccer with a buddy every Saturday.

en kammerjunker.explanation: "En kammerjunker" means "a small Danish cookie", a small, dry, crunchy cookie that is eaten as a snack. The name sounds like a title, but it is only a cookie.

sentence.da: Han dypper sin **kammerjunker** i kaffen, så den bliver blød.
sentence.en: He dips his cookie in the coffee so it gets soft.

en kamp.explanation: "En kamp" means "a match" or "a game" in sports: en fodboldkamp (a soccer game). It can also mean "a fight" or "a struggle": en kamp mod kræft (a fight against cancer).

sentence.da: Holdet har en **kamp** mod Brøndby i aften.
sentence.en: The team has a match against Brøndby tonight.

en kampagne.explanation: "En kampagne" means "a campaign", a planned effort to reach a goal in ads or politics: Firmaet starter en ny kampagne (The company is starting a new campaign). It can also be a sale: en tilbudskampagne (a sale campaign).

sentence.da: Partiet har en stor **kampagne** før valget.
sentence.en: The party has a big campaign before the election.

en kanal.explanation: "En kanal" means "a channel" on TV or online: Hvilken kanal ser du? (Which channel are you watching?). It can also mean a water canal, so the situation tells you which one.

sentence.da: Jeg skifter til en anden **kanal**.
sentence.en: I switch to another channel.

en kanalrundfart.explanation: "En kanalrundfart" means "a canal tour", a sightseeing ride on the water through the canals of a city. It is built from kanal (canal) and rundfart (a sightseeing loop). Kanal also means a channel: en tv-kanal (a TV channel).

sentence.da: Vi sejler gennem byen på en **kanalrundfart**.
sentence.en: We sail through the city on a canal tour.

en kandidat.explanation: "En kandidat" means "a candidate", a person who stands for election or is considered for a job. At a university, it also means someone with a master's degree, which comes after the first degree.

sentence.da: Hver **kandidat** får ti minutter til at tale om sine planer.
sentence.en: Each candidate gets ten minutes to talk about their plans.

en kanelsnegl.explanation: "En kanelsnegl" means "a cinnamon roll". It is built from kanel (cinnamon) and en snegl (a snail), because the roll is curled like a snail shell.

sentence.da: Min **kanelsnegl** er sød og smager af kanel.
sentence.en: My cinnamon roll is sweet and tastes of cinnamon.

en kanin.explanation: "En kanin" means "a rabbit", a small furry animal with a short tail that people keep as a pet. Do not mix it up with en hare (a hare), which is bigger and lives wild.

sentence.da: En **kanin** har lange ører og hopper rundt.
sentence.en: A rabbit has long ears and hops around.

en kano.explanation: "En kano" means "a canoe", a light, narrow boat that you move with a short oar. Danish uses at sejle (to sail) for any trip on water: sejle i kano (to go canoeing).

sentence.da: Vi kan leje en **kano** og sejle på søen.
sentence.en: We can rent a canoe and paddle on the lake.

en kanon.explanation: "En kanon" means "a cannon", a large old gun on wheels or on a ship. In everyday talk, kanon is also slang for something great: Filmen var kanon (The film was great).

sentence.da: En **kanon** skyder tunge kugler ud af et langt metalrør.
sentence.en: A cannon shoots heavy balls out of a long metal tube.

en kant.explanation: "En kant" means "an edge", the outer line or limit of something: Glasset står på kanten af bordet (The glass is on the edge of the table).

sentence.da: Pas på, bordet har en skarp **kant**.
sentence.en: Watch out, the table has a sharp edge.

en kantine.explanation: "En kantine" means "a canteen", where you buy lunch at a school or workplace. A restaurant (en restaurant) is open to everyone, but a kantine is usually for the people who work or study there.

sentence.da: Skolen har en **kantine**, og vi køber frokost der.
sentence.en: The school has a canteen, and we buy lunch there.

en kantsten.explanation: "En kantsten" means "a curb", the raised stone edge at the side of a street. It is built from kant (edge) and sten (stone). Kant works for any edge: kanten af bordet (the edge of the table).

sentence.da: Cyklen kørte ind i en **kantsten** og væltede.
sentence.en: The bike hit a curb and fell.

en kappe.explanation: "En kappe" means "a cloak" or "a robe", a long, loose piece of clothing that hangs from the shoulders, such as a judge's robe or a superhero's cloak.

sentence.da: Munken har en lang **kappe** med hætte på.
sentence.en: The monk is wearing a long robe with a hood.

en kaptajn.explanation: "En kaptajn" means "a captain", the person in charge of a ship or a plane. It is also an army rank, and the captain of a sports team is called en anfører.

sentence.da: Hvert skib har en **kaptajn**, som bestemmer, hvor det sejler.
sentence.en: Every ship has a captain who decides where it sails.

en karakter.explanation: "En karakter" means "a grade" at school: Jeg fik en god karakter (I got a good grade). It also means "a character" in a story, or a person's nature: Hun har en stærk karakter (She has a strong character).

sentence.da: Læreren giver mig en **karakter** for opgaven.
sentence.en: The teacher gives me a grade for the assignment.

en karamel.explanation: "En karamel" means "a caramel", a chewy sweet. With sovs (sauce) it becomes a topping: karamelsovs (caramel sauce).

sentence.da: En **karamel** er sød og sej og smager af smør.
sentence.en: A caramel is sweet and chewy and tastes of butter.

en karikatur.explanation: "En karikatur" means "a caricature", a funny picture of a person that makes certain features much bigger than they really are. Newspapers often print caricatures of politicians.

sentence.da: Avisen har en **karikatur** af statsministeren med en kæmpestor næse.
sentence.en: The newspaper has a caricature of the prime minister with a giant nose.

en karriere.explanation: "En karriere" means "a career", your work path over many years: Hun har en lang karriere bag sig (She has a long career behind her). To build one, say at gøre karriere (to make a career).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne have en **karriere** som læge.
sentence.en: She would like to have a career as a doctor.

en kartoffel.explanation: "En kartoffel" means "a potato", a round vegetable that grows in the ground and is eaten boiled or fried.

sentence.da: Jeg skræller en **kartoffel** og koger den.
sentence.en: I peel a potato and boil it.

en karton.explanation: "En karton" means "a carton", the cardboard container that holds drinks such as milk or juice. It also forms longer words: en æggekarton (an egg carton).

sentence.da: Mælk og juice kommer ofte i en **karton**.
sentence.en: Milk and juice often come in a carton.

en kasket.explanation: "En kasket" means "a cap", the kind with a peak at the front, like a baseball cap. It is not en hue (a knit wool hat) or en hat (a hat with a brim).

sentence.da: Han har en **kasket** med skygge på hovedet.
sentence.en: He has a cap with a visor on his head.

en kasse.explanation: "En kasse" means "a box", and also "the checkout" in a store: Betal ved kassen (Pay at the checkout). For a small gift box, Danes say en æske (a small box).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger bøgerne i en stor **kasse**.
sentence.en: I put the books in a big box.

en kassebon.explanation: "En kassebon" means "a register receipt", the slip you get when you pay in a store. You need it if you want to return or exchange something.

related.en: a complaint about a faulty item

sentence.da: Jeg vil bytte varen, men jeg har ikke min **kassebon**.
sentence.en: I want to exchange the item, but I do not have my receipt.

en kassedame.explanation: "En kassedame" means "a cashier", the person at the register in a store. Literally it is register lady, so en kassemedarbejder (a register employee) is a more neutral choice.

sentence.da: Hun arbejder som **kassedame** i en butik.
sentence.en: She works as a cashier in a store.

en kassemedarbejder.explanation: "En kassemedarbejder" means "a cashier", the person at the checkout in a store who rings up what you buy and takes your payment. The word is the same for a man or a woman.

sentence.da: En **kassemedarbejder** scanner varerne og tager imod betalingen.
sentence.en: A cashier scans the goods and takes the payment.

en kasserolle.explanation: "En kasserolle" means "a saucepan", a deep metal cooking dish with one long handle, used for sauce, rice and soup.

sentence.da: Jeg varmer suppen i en **kasserolle**.
sentence.en: I heat the soup in a saucepan.

en kastanje.explanation: "En kastanje" means "a chestnut", a shiny brown nut that falls from a tree in autumn. The ones in Danish parks are mostly hestekastanjer (horse chestnuts), which are not for eating. The ones you roast and eat are ægte kastanjer (sweet chestnuts).

sentence.da: Om efteråret falder en **kastanje** ned fra træet med et bump.
sentence.en: In the fall, a chestnut drops from the tree with a thud.

en kat.explanation: "En kat" means "a cat", the small furry pet that purrs and chases mice.

sentence.da: Min **kat** siger mjav og drikker mælk.
sentence.en: My cat says meow and drinks milk.

en katastrofe.explanation: "En katastrofe" means "a disaster", something very bad or a big failure: Festen var en katastrofe (The party was a disaster). It is also used for natural events: en naturkatastrofe (a natural disaster).

sentence.da: Oversvømmelsen var en **katastrofe** for byen.
sentence.en: The flood was a disaster for the town.

en katedral.explanation: "En katedral" means "a cathedral", a very large and important church, usually the main church of a region where a bishop is based.

sentence.da: En **katedral** er større end en almindelig kirke.
sentence.en: A cathedral is bigger than an ordinary church.

en kategori.explanation: "En kategori" means "a category", a label for sorting similar things, such as the topics in a word list.

sentence.da: Frugt er en **kategori** af mad.
sentence.en: Fruit is a category of food.

en kattebakke.explanation: "En kattebakke" means "a litter box", a tray that an indoor cat uses as a toilet. It is built from kat (cat) and bakke (tray). Bakke also means a hill, so the context tells you which: Vi går op ad en bakke (We walk up a hill).

sentence.da: Katten bruger sin **kattebakke**, når den skal på toilet.
sentence.en: The cat uses its litter box when it needs the toilet.

en kaution.explanation: "En kaution" means "a bail" or "a guarantee": money put down as a pledge that you will do something. In court, it lets a suspect wait at home until the trial. It is also the money you pay up front when renting a home.

sentence.da: Hun betalte en **kaution** for at slippe ud af fængslet.
sentence.en: She paid bail to get out of jail.

en kejser.explanation: "En kejser" means "an emperor", the highest leader of a large, powerful state. A woman in that role is en kejserinde. The word also appears in et kejsersnit (a C-section).

sentence.da: Romerrigets **kejser** boede i et stort palads i Rom.
sentence.en: The emperor of the Roman Empire lived in a large palace in Rome.

en kemiker.explanation: "En kemiker" means "a chemist", a scientist who studies what substances are made of and how they react. Watch out: it is not a drugstore worker as in British English. For that, use en apoteker (a pharmacist).

sentence.da: En **kemiker** blander to væsker for at se, hvad der sker.
sentence.en: A chemist mixes two liquids to see what happens.

en kendelse.explanation: "En kendelse" means "a ruling", an official finding by a court. It is also the word for a warrant, an order that lets police search a place.

sentence.da: Politiet må have en **kendelse**, før de kan gennemsøge huset.
sentence.en: The police must have a warrant before they can search the house.

en kerne.explanation: "En kerne" means "a core" or "a kernel", the most important inner part of something. It also means a seed inside a fruit, as in æblekerner (apple seeds), and the nucleus of a cell or an atom.

sentence.da: Problemets **kerne** er, at vi ikke har penge nok.
sentence.en: The core of the problem is that we do not have enough money.

en ketsjer.explanation: "En ketsjer" means "a racket", the frame with strings that you hold in tennis, badminton and squash.

sentence.da: Man slår til bolden med en **ketsjer** i tennis.
sentence.en: You hit the ball with a racket in tennis.

en kidnapning.explanation: "En kidnapning" means "a kidnapping", taking someone away against their will, often to demand money. To kidnap someone, say at kidnappe.

sentence.da: Politiet undersøger en **kidnapning** af en rig forretningsmand.
sentence.en: The police are investigating the kidnapping of a rich businessman.

en kikkert.explanation: "En kikkert" means "a pair of binoculars", used to see things far away. Danish says one kikkert where English says a pair.

sentence.da: Med en **kikkert** kan jeg se fuglen langt væk.
sentence.en: With binoculars I can see the bird far away.

en kiks.explanation: "En kiks" means "a biscuit" or "a cracker". En småkage (a small sweet cookie) is a different thing.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **kiks** med ost.
sentence.en: I eat a cracker with cheese.

en kilde.explanation: "En kilde" means "a source": Hvad er din kilde? (What is your source?) It also means "a spring", where water comes out of the ground: en kilde i bjergene (a spring in the mountains).

sentence.da: Vandet kommer fra en **kilde** i skoven.
sentence.en: The water comes from a spring in the forest.

en killing.explanation: "En killing" means "a kitten", a young cat. The grown-up animal is en kat (a cat).

sentence.da: Vores kat har fået en lille **killing**.
sentence.en: Our cat has had a little kitten.

en kilometer.explanation: "En kilometer" means "a kilometer", which is 1,000 meters. Speed is measured in kilometer i timen (kilometers per hour).

sentence.da: Der er tre **kilometer** til stationen.
sentence.en: It is three kilometers to the station.

en kind.explanation: "En kind" means "a cheek", the soft, round part on each side of your face under the eye. Røde kinder (red cheeks) show cold or a blush.

sentence.da: Hun giver mig et kys på min **kind**.
sentence.en: She gives me a kiss on my cheek.

en kineser.explanation: "En kineser" means "a Chinese person": Hun er kineser (She is Chinese). For things from China, use kinesisk: kinesisk mad (Chinese food).

sentence.da: Min læge er **kineser**, men hun taler godt dansk.
sentence.en: My doctor is Chinese, but she speaks good Danish.

en kiosk.explanation: "En kiosk" means "a kiosk", a small shop that sells drinks, sweets, newspapers and snacks. It is smaller than et supermarked (a supermarket).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en avis i en **kiosk**.
sentence.en: I buy a newspaper at a kiosk.

en kirke.explanation: "En kirke" means "a church", a building where people hold services, weddings and funerals. Do not confuse it with en kirkegård (a cemetery), a place with graves.

sentence.da: Folk beder og synger i en **kirke**.
sentence.en: People pray and sing in a church.

en kirkegård.explanation: "En kirkegård" means "a cemetery", the place where the dead are buried, usually next to a church. It is built from kirke (church) and gård (yard). Gård alone means a farm or a yard: en gård på landet (a farm in the country).

sentence.da: Der er mange grave på den gamle **kirkegård**.
sentence.en: There are many graves in the old cemetery.

en kirurg.explanation: "En kirurg" means "a surgeon", a medical specialist who treats illness and injury by cutting into the body. The work itself is called kirurgi (surgery).

sentence.da: En **kirurg** kan fjerne blindtarmen, hvis den er betændt.
sentence.en: A surgeon can remove the appendix if it is inflamed.

en kiste.explanation: "En kiste" means "a chest", a large container with a lid, for example for treasure or old clothes. It is also the usual word for a coffin.

sentence.da: Skatten lå gemt i en gammel **kiste** under jorden.
sentence.en: The treasure lay hidden in an old chest under the ground.

en kiwi.explanation: "En kiwi" means "a kiwi", a small fruit with fuzzy brown skin.

sentence.da: En **kiwi** er grøn indeni og har små sorte kerner.
sentence.en: A kiwi is green inside and has small black seeds.

en kjole.explanation: "En kjole" means "a dress", a piece of clothing for women and girls that covers the body and part of the legs. You can build words from it, such as en festkjole (a party dress) and en sommerkjole (a summer dress).

sentence.da: Hun har en lang **kjole** på til festen.
sentence.en: She is wearing a long dress to the party.

en klage.explanation: "En klage" means "a complaint": Jeg har en klage over maden (I have a complaint about the food). To complain is at klage over (to complain about).

sentence.da: Vi sendte en **klage** til firmaet.
sentence.en: We sent a complaint to the company.

en klapvogn.explanation: "En klapvogn" means "a stroller", the light folding kind where the child sits up. For a newborn who lies down, use en barnevogn (a baby carriage).

sentence.da: Jeg kan folde min **klapvogn** sammen.
sentence.en: I can fold my stroller up.

en klasse.explanation: "En klasse" means "a class", both the group of pupils and the classroom. Danish schools count the school years as classes: 2. klasse means "second grade".

sentence.da: Der er tyve børn i min **klasse**.
sentence.en: There are twenty children in my class.

en klassekammerat.explanation: "En klassekammerat" means "a classmate". It is built from klasse (class) and kammerat (pal). Kammerat also appears in en holdkammerat (a teammate), someone in the same team as you.

sentence.da: Min **klassekammerat** hjælper mig med lektierne.
sentence.en: My classmate helps me with the homework.

en klasselærer.explanation: "En klasselærer" means "a class teacher", the teacher who looks after one class, often stays with it for years and is the main contact for each child's home.

sentence.da: Min **klasselærer** ringede til mine forældre, da jeg var syg.
sentence.en: My class teacher called my parents when I was sick.

en klassificering.explanation: "En klassificering" means "a classification", putting things into groups by what they have in common. To do this, say at klassificere (to classify).

sentence.da: Biologer arbejder med **klassificering** af levende ting i arter.
sentence.en: Biologists work with the classification of living things into species.

en klassiker.explanation: "En klassiker" means "a classic", something very well known that has lasted for many years, such as a book, a film or a song. It also fits a dish or a design that never goes out of style. For classical music, say klassisk musik.

sentence.da: Den gamle film er blevet en **klassiker**, som alle har set.
sentence.en: The old film has become a classic that everyone has seen.

en klat.explanation: "En klat" means "a dollop" or "a blob", a small, soft bit of something thick or sticky that lands in one go. You say what it is made of: en klat maling (a blob of paint).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **klat** smør på brødet.
sentence.en: I put a dollop of butter on the bread.

en klejne.explanation: "En klejne" means "a Christmas cruller", a twisted strip of dough that is fried in fat. It is a traditional Danish Christmas treat.

sentence.da: Til jul spiser vi en sprød **klejne** med kaffe.
sentence.en: At Christmas we eat a crisp cruller with coffee.

en klemme.explanation: "En klemme" means "a clothespin" or "a clip", a small tool with a spring that holds things together. It also means a hug: Giv mig en klemme (Give me a hug).

sentence.da: Hver sok hænger på snoren med en **klemme**.
sentence.en: Each sock hangs on the line with a clothespin.

en klient.explanation: "En klient" means "a client", a person who gets advice or help from a professional, such as a lawyer. In a shop or café, you are not a klient but en kunde (a customer).

sentence.da: Advokaten møder sin **klient** i morgen klokken ti.
sentence.en: The lawyer meets her client tomorrow at ten.

en klinik.explanation: "En klinik" means "a clinic", a place where you see a doctor or dentist without staying overnight. A hospital, where people can stay overnight, is et sygehus or "et hospital".

sentence.da: Jeg ser en læge på en **klinik**.
sentence.en: I see a doctor at a clinic.

en klipning.explanation: "En klipning" means "a haircut", the act of getting your hair shortened or shaped. The look itself is called en frisure (a hairstyle).

sentence.da: Jeg har booket en **klipning**, fordi mit hår er blevet for langt.
sentence.en: I booked a haircut because my hair has gotten too long.

en klippe.explanation: "En klippe" means "a cliff" or "a big rock" in nature. A small rock you can pick up is en sten (a stone). The same spelling is also at klippe (to cut): Jeg klipper papir (I cut paper).

sentence.da: Vi sad på en stor **klippe** og så på havet.
sentence.en: We sat on a big rock and looked at the sea.

en klit.explanation: "En klit" means "a sand dune", a heap of sand shaped by the wind along the coast. It is often held in place by tough grass.

sentence.da: Vinden har blæst sandet op til en høj **klit**.
sentence.en: The wind has blown the sand up into a tall dune.

en klo.explanation: "En klo" means "a claw", the hard, sharp nail on an animal's paw or a bird's foot, and also the pincer of a crab. It appears in the saying at komme i kløerne på nogen (to fall into someone's clutches).

sentence.da: En ørn har en skarp **klo** på hver tå.
sentence.en: An eagle has a sharp claw on each toe.

en klode.explanation: "En klode" means "a planet", but it is used mostly for our own: kloden (the Earth). For the other planets, say en planet (a planet). Vi rejser rundt på kloden (We travel all around the Earth).

sentence.da: Der bor otte milliarder mennesker på vores **klode**.
sentence.en: Eight billion people live on our planet.

en klods.explanation: "En klods" means "a block", like a toy block or a chunk of wood. Lego bricks are legoklodser (Lego blocks).

sentence.da: Hun sætter en **klods** oven på tårnet.
sentence.en: She puts a block on top of the tower.

en klokke.explanation: "En klokke" means "a bell": Klokken ringer (The bell is ringing). The same word is used for telling time: Hvad er klokken? (What time is it?)

sentence.da: Jeg hører en **klokke** ringe i kirken.
sentence.en: I hear a bell ring in the church.

en klovn.explanation: "En klovn" means "a clown", the funny performer in colorful clothes. It can also mean a silly person: Du er en klovn (You are a clown).

sentence.da: Den sjove **klovn** har en stor rød næse.
sentence.en: The funny clown has a big red nose.

en klub.explanation: "En klub" means "a club", a group that meets for a shared activity: Jeg er med i en fodboldklub (I am in a soccer club). It also means a nightclub: Vi går i klub i aften (We are going clubbing tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg spiller skak i en **klub** hver torsdag.
sentence.en: I play chess in a club every Thursday.

en klud.explanation: "En klud" means "a cloth" or "a rag" for cleaning. For drying plates, you use et viskestykke (a dish towel).

sentence.da: Tag en **klud**, og tør vandet op!
sentence.en: Take a cloth and wipe up the water!

en klump.explanation: "En klump" means "a lump", a solid piece without a clear shape: en klump ler (a lump of clay). Suppen er fuld af klumper (The soup is full of lumps).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **klump** smør og smelter den i panden.
sentence.en: I take a lump of butter and melt it in the pan.

en kløver.explanation: "En kløver" means "a clover", a low plant with three small round leaves. A clover with four leaves is called en firkløver and is said to bring luck.

sentence.da: Der vokser hvid **kløver** i plænen hele sommeren.
sentence.en: White clover grows in the lawn all summer.

en knage.explanation: "En knage" means "a coat hook", a small hook fixed to a wall or door where you hang coats, hats and bags. It is a common sight in a hallway.

sentence.da: Jeg hænger min jakke på en **knage** i gangen.
sentence.en: I hang my jacket on a coat hook in the hallway.

en knallert.explanation: "En knallert" means "a moped", a small, light motorbike with a low top speed of about 45 km/h, used for short trips.

sentence.da: En **knallert** er langsommere end en motorcykel.
sentence.en: A moped is slower than a motorcycle.

en knap.explanation: "En knap" means "a button", on clothes and on a machine: Tryk på knappen (Press the button). Without en, knap means "barely": Der er knap tid (There is barely any time).

sentence.da: Der mangler en **knap** på min jakke.
sentence.en: A button is missing on my jacket.

en knibe.explanation: "En knibe" means "a fix", a difficult situation that is hard to escape. It almost always appears as i knibe (in a fix), without en.

forms.en: to help someone out of a fix

sentence.da: Jeg er i **knibe**, fordi jeg har mistet min nøgle.
sentence.en: I am in a fix because I have lost my key.

en kniv.explanation: "En kniv" means "a knife", the tool with a sharp blade for cutting food. At the table it comes with en gaffel (a fork): kniv og gaffel (knife and fork).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer brød med en **kniv**.
sentence.en: I cut bread with a knife.

en knivspids.explanation: "En knivspids" means "a pinch", built from en kniv (a knife) and en spids (a tip): the tiny amount that fits on the tip of a knife. Recipes use it for spices and salt.

sentence.da: Tilføj en **knivspids** salt til suppen.
sentence.en: Add a pinch of salt to the soup.

en knogle.explanation: "En knogle" means "a bone", one of the hard parts that make up the body's frame. In food, a bone is often called et ben, which also means a leg.

sentence.da: Røntgen viser, om en **knogle** er brækket.
sentence.en: The X-ray shows whether a bone is broken.

en knop.explanation: "En knop" means "a bud", the small closed part of a plant that later opens into a flower or leaf. Do not mix it up with en knap (a button).

sentence.da: Træet har en lille **knop**, som åbner sig i morgen.
sentence.en: The tree has a small bud that opens tomorrow.

en knude.explanation: "En knude" means "a knot", in a rope or in hair: en knude i håret (a knot in the hair). It is also used for a tight spot in a muscle: en knude i nakken (a knot in the neck).

sentence.da: Der er en **knude** på rebet.
sentence.en: There is a knot in the rope.

en knægt.explanation: "En knægt" means "a lad" or "a kid", a warm word for a young male: Sikke en dejlig knægt! (What a lovely lad!).

sentence.da: Han er kun otte, men han er en stærk **knægt**.
sentence.en: He is only eight, but he is a strong lad.

en ko.explanation: "En ko" means "a cow", a large farm animal kept for its milk and meat. It lives on a farm and spends the summer in a field.

sentence.da: En **ko** spiser græs på marken.
sentence.en: A cow eats grass in the field.

en koalition.explanation: "En koalition" means "a coalition", several groups joining forces to reach a goal together. In Danish politics, it means several political groups that govern together because none has enough votes alone.

sentence.da: Den nye regering er en **koalition** mellem tre partier.
sentence.en: The new government is a coalition between three parties.

en kobling.explanation: "En kobling" means "a clutch", the pedal in a manual car that you press to change gears. It also means a link between two things, like the coupling between two train cars.

sentence.da: Bilen har en **kobling**, så man kan skifte gear.
sentence.en: The car has a clutch so that you can change gears.

en kode.explanation: "En kode" means "a code", letters or numbers that open or identify something: Skriv koden på skærmen (Type the code on the screen). It also means computer code: Han skriver kode (He writes code).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge en **kode** for at åbne døren.
sentence.en: You need a code to open the door.

en kofanger.explanation: "En kofanger" means "a bumper", the bar at the front and back of a car that takes the hit in a small crash.

sentence.da: Der er en bule i min **kofanger**.
sentence.en: There is a dent in my bumper.

en kogeplade.explanation: "En kogeplade" means "a hotplate", the heated plate you cook on. It is built from at koge (to boil) and en plade (a plate). The verb works for food in water: Jeg koger kartofler (I boil potatoes).

sentence.da: Jeg stiller den varme gryde på en **kogeplade**.
sentence.en: I put the hot pot on a hotplate.

en kogle.explanation: "En kogle" means "a pine cone", the hard, scaly case that holds the seeds of a pine tree. It is also used for the cones of other evergreens.

sentence.da: Hver **kogle** på træet gemmer små frø mellem skællene.
sentence.en: Each cone on the tree hides small seeds between its scales.

en kogning.explanation: "En kogning" means "a boiling", the process of cooking something in boiling water. In everyday talk, Danes more often say at koge (to boil) or use et kog (a boil): Bring det i kog (Bring it to a boil).

sentence.da: Efter **kogning** skal pastaen køle lidt af.
sentence.en: After boiling, the pasta needs to cool a little.

en kok.explanation: "En kok" means "a chef" or "a cook". Do not mix it up with at koge (to boil): a kok is the person, koge is what the pot does.

sentence.da: Min bror er **kok** på en restaurant.
sentence.en: My brother is a chef at a restaurant.

en kokkeelev.explanation: "En kokkeelev" means "a chef apprentice", someone who is learning to be a cook. It is built from en kok (a cook) and en elev (a pupil). Elev also appears in en skoleelev (a school pupil).

sentence.da: Som **kokkeelev** lærer jeg at lave mad på en restaurant.
sentence.en: As a chef apprentice, I learn to cook at a restaurant.

en koldskål.explanation: "En koldskål" means "a cold buttermilk dessert", a cold, sweet Danish dish made of buttermilk that you eat from a bowl, mostly in summer. It is often served with small crisp cookies called kammerjunkere.

sentence.da: Efter en varm dag smager en **koldskål** dejligt.
sentence.en: After a hot day, a koldskål tastes lovely.

en kollega.explanation: "En kollega" means "a colleague", a person you work with at the same workplace, usually at a similar level.

sentence.da: Min **kollega** og jeg arbejder sammen på kontoret.
sentence.en: My colleague and I work together in the office.

en kolonihave.explanation: "En kolonihave" means "an allotment garden", a small piece of land with a little house that city people rent in an area shared with many others. Many families spend summer weekends there.

sentence.da: Min familie har en **kolonihave**, hvor vi dyrker grøntsager.
sentence.en: My family has an allotment garden where we grow vegetables.

en kombination.explanation: "En kombination" means "a combination", two or more things together: en kombination af sødt og surt (a combination of sweet and sour). It is also the set of numbers that opens a lock: Jeg glemte kombinationen (I forgot the combination).

sentence.da: Pasta og ost er en god **kombination**.
sentence.en: Pasta and cheese are a good combination.

en komedie.explanation: "En komedie" means "a comedy", a film, play or TV show made to make you laugh. The opposite is en tragedie (a tragedy), which ends sadly.

sentence.da: Vi griner hele aftenen, fordi filmen er en **komedie**.
sentence.en: We laugh all evening because the film is a comedy.

en komet.explanation: "En komet" means "a comet", a lump of ice and dust that moves around the sun and glows brightly when it comes close.

sentence.da: Vi kan se en **komet** med en lang hale på himlen.
sentence.en: We can see a comet with a long tail in the sky.

en komiker.explanation: "En komiker" means "a comedian", a person who makes people laugh on stage, on TV or online. One who tells jokes alone on a stage is called en stand-up-komiker (a stand-up comedian).

sentence.da: En **komiker** står på scenen og får publikum til at le.
sentence.en: A comedian stands on the stage and makes the audience laugh.

en kommando.explanation: "En kommando" means "a command", a short, firm call to do something that must be obeyed, for example from an officer to soldiers. In computing, it is a line you type to make a program do something.

sentence.da: Hunden sætter sig på **kommando**.
sentence.en: The dog sits on command.

en kommandør.explanation: "En kommandør" means "a commander", a high-ranking leader of a military unit. As an official rank, it is used in the navy.

sentence.da: En **kommandør** leder en stor styrke af soldater og skibe.
sentence.en: A commander leads a large force of soldiers and ships.

en kommentar.explanation: "En kommentar" means "a comment", something you write or say about a thing, often under a post or a video. The action is at kommentere (to comment).

sentence.da: Jeg læste hver **kommentar** under opslaget.
sentence.en: I read every comment under the post.

en kommentator.explanation: "En kommentator" means "a commentator", someone who describes and gives opinions on events, for example a sports match on TV or the news in a newspaper column.

sentence.da: En **kommentator** forklarer, hvad der sker i kampen.
sentence.en: A commentator explains what is happening in the match.

en kommissær.explanation: "En kommissær" means "a commissioner", a high official in charge of one special area, for example in the EU. In the police, en politikommissær is a senior officer who leads an investigation.

sentence.da: En **kommissær** i EU har ansvar for et bestemt område.
sentence.en: A commissioner in the EU is responsible for a certain area.

en kommode.explanation: "En kommode" means "a chest of drawers", a low piece of furniture with several drawers stacked on top of each other, often in a bedroom for clothes.

sentence.da: Mit tøj ligger i en hvid **kommode**.
sentence.en: My clothes are in a white chest of drawers.

en kommune.explanation: "En kommune" means "a municipality", the local area and its government, which runs things like schools, libraries and care for older people.

sentence.da: Vores **kommune** bygger en ny skole.
sentence.en: Our municipality is building a new school.

en komponist.explanation: "En komponist" means "a composer", a person who writes music for instruments, singers or film. The ending -ist marks a person in many Danish words, as in en pianist (a pianist) and en turist (a tourist).

sentence.da: En **komponist** skriver noder, som andre senere spiller.
sentence.en: A composer writes sheet music that others play later.

en koncentration.explanation: "En koncentration" means "a concentration", the ability to keep your mind on one thing. It also tells how much of a substance is in a mix, such as salt in water.

sentence.da: Det kræver **koncentration** at læse i et støjende rum.
sentence.en: It takes concentration to read in a noisy room.

en koncert.explanation: "En koncert" means "a concert", a live music show by a singer, a band or an orchestra. At gå til koncert means "to go to a concert", and Danish leaves out the word for "a" there.

sentence.da: Bandet spiller mange sange på en **koncert**.
sentence.en: The band plays many songs at a concert.

en kondicykel.explanation: "En kondicykel" means "an exercise bike", a bike that stays in one place indoors. Kondi is short for kondition, the word for how fit you are: Jeg har god kondition (I have good stamina).

sentence.da: Når det regner, træner jeg på min **kondicykel** i stuen.
sentence.en: When it rains, I work out on my exercise bike in the living room.

en kondolence.explanation: "En kondolence" means "a condolence", words of comfort to someone who has lost a loved one. You say it as min kondolence (my condolences) or write it in a card.

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig min dybfølte **kondolence** efter dødsfaldet.
sentence.en: I am sending you my deepest condolences after the death.

en kone.explanation: "En kone" means "a wife". For a woman in general, use en kvinde (a woman), not kone, which only means a married partner.

sentence.da: Han giftede sig med sin **kone** i 2010.
sentence.en: He married his wife in 2010.

en konfirmation.explanation: "En konfirmation" means "a confirmation", a Christian ceremony for teenagers, usually at age 14, followed by a big family party.

sentence.da: Min lillebror har **konfirmation** i foråret.
sentence.en: My little brother has his confirmation in the spring.

en konflikt.explanation: "En konflikt" means "a conflict", a serious fight between people, groups or countries. It can be small, like a quarrel at work, or large, like a war.

sentence.da: Der er opstået en **konflikt** mellem de to naboer om hækken.
sentence.en: A conflict has arisen between the two neighbors over the hedge.

en konge.explanation: "En konge" means "a king", the male ruler of a country. The king's wife is en dronning (a queen).

sentence.da: En **konge** styrer et land.
sentence.en: A king rules a country.

en konklusion.explanation: "En konklusion" means "a conclusion", what you decide is true after thinking about the facts. It is also the last part of a text or report, where the main points are gathered.

sentence.da: Efter mange tests kom forskerne til en **konklusion**.
sentence.en: After many tests, the researchers came to a conclusion.

en konkurrence.explanation: "En konkurrence" means "a competition", where people try to win. The verb is at konkurrere (to compete), and a rival is en konkurrent (a competitor).

sentence.da: Man kan vinde en pris i en **konkurrence**.
sentence.en: You can win a prize in a competition.

en konkurrent.explanation: "En konkurrent" means "a competitor", a person or company that tries to win the same customers or prizes as you.

sentence.da: Vores **konkurrent** sælger de samme varer til lavere priser.
sentence.en: Our competitor sells the same goods at lower prices.

en konsekvens.explanation: "En konsekvens" means "a consequence", what happens because of something you did or something that happened. The related word konsekvent means doing what you said every time (consistent).

sentence.da: Hans træthed er en **konsekvens** af for lidt søvn.
sentence.en: His tiredness is a consequence of too little sleep.

en konsistens.explanation: "En konsistens" means "a texture", how firm, runny or smooth a food or liquid is. Watch out: English "consistency" can mean doing the same each time, but in Danish that is konsekvent.

sentence.da: Budding har en blød og glat **konsistens**.
sentence.en: Pudding has a soft and smooth texture.

en konsonant.explanation: "En konsonant" means "a consonant", such as b, d or k. The opposite is en vokal (a vowel).

sentence.da: I ordet bog er b en **konsonant** og o en vokal.
sentence.en: In the word bog, b is a consonant and o is a vowel.

en konsulent.explanation: "En konsulent" means "a consultant", someone with deep knowledge whom a company hires to give advice on a specific job or problem, usually for a limited time. Many consultants work for themselves instead of having one employer.

sentence.da: Firmaet har hyret en **konsulent** til at give råd om økonomien.
sentence.en: The company has hired a consultant to give advice about the finances.

en kontakt.explanation: "En kontakt" means "a contact" and also "a switch": Jeg har en kontakt i banken (I have a contact at the bank). Kontakten er ved døren (The switch is by the door).

sentence.da: Jeg har stadig **kontakt** med min gamle ven.
sentence.en: I still have contact with my old friend.

en kontaktlinse.explanation: "En kontaktlinse" means "a contact lens", a thin lens you wear directly on the eye instead of in a frame.

sentence.da: Hun har en **kontaktlinse** i hvert øje i stedet for briller.
sentence.en: She has a contact lens in each eye instead of glasses.

en kontaktløs betaling.explanation: "En kontaktløs betaling" means "a contactless payment", where you hold your phone or bank card close to the terminal instead of inserting it. Small purchases are often made this way.

sentence.da: Ved **kontaktløs betaling** holder du bare telefonen ind til terminalen.
sentence.en: With contactless payment you just hold the phone up to the terminal.

en kontaktperson.explanation: "En kontaktperson" means "a contact person", someone you call or write to first, for example at a school or a workplace. The word is the same for a man and a woman: Han er vores kontaktperson (He is our contact person).

sentence.da: Min **kontaktperson** på skolen hedder Anne.
sentence.en: My contact person at the school is called Anne.

en kontekst.explanation: "En kontekst" means "a context", the words or circumstances around something that show what it really means. A word or sentence can mean something else when it is taken out of its context.

sentence.da: Uden **kontekst** kan man ikke se, hvad ordet betyder.
sentence.en: Without context you cannot tell what the word means.

en konto.explanation: "En konto" means "an account", a place where a bank keeps your money, or where you log in online.

sentence.da: Jeg sætter penge ind på min **konto**.
sentence.en: I put money into my account.

en kontorassistent.explanation: "En kontorassistent" means "an office assistant", a person who does everyday office tasks such as answering the phone, filing papers and ordering supplies. It is a general job title for office support.

sentence.da: Vi har ansat en ny **kontorassistent** til at hjælpe på kontoret.
sentence.en: We have hired a new office assistant to help in the office.
