en kontorplads.explanation: "En kontorplads" means "a desk (workspace)", your own place to sit and work at a company, often one seat in a shared room. People often say how many they need: Vi mangler tre kontorpladser (We are short of three workspaces).

sentence.da: Min nye **kontorplads** er ved vinduet, så jeg har dagslys.
sentence.en: My new workspace is by the window, so I have daylight.

en kontorstol.explanation: "En kontorstol" means "an office chair", built from kontor (office) and stol (chair). For "at the office" Danish uses på: Jeg er på kontoret (I am at the office).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder på en god **kontorstol** hele dagen.
sentence.en: I sit on a good office chair all day.

en kontrakt.explanation: "En kontrakt" means "a contract", a written agreement with fixed terms between two sides, for example for a job or a home. A spoken deal is just en aftale (an agreement).

sentence.da: Før du skriver under, skal du læse hele din **kontrakt**.
sentence.en: Before you sign, you must read your whole contract.

en kontrast.explanation: "En kontrast" means "a contrast", a clear difference between two things placed side by side, such as light and dark. It also works for ideas: i kontrast til (in contrast to).

sentence.da: Der er stor **kontrast** mellem den lyse væg og det sorte gulv.
sentence.en: There is a big contrast between the light wall and the black floor.

en kontrol.explanation: "En kontrol" means "a check", for example by the police or at a border: Der er kontrol i lufthavnen (There is a check at the airport). It also means "control": Han har kontrol over bilen (He has control of the car).

sentence.da: Politiet laver en **kontrol** på vejen.
sentence.en: The police are doing a check on the road.

en kontrolafgift.explanation: "En kontrolafgift" means "a penalty fare", the extra money you must pay if you ride without a valid ticket. It is built from kontrol (check) and afgift (fee).

sentence.da: Uden billet får du en **kontrolafgift**.
sentence.en: Without a ticket, you get a penalty fare.

en koordinat.explanation: "En koordinat" means "a coordinate", one of the numbers that give an exact place on a map or in a graph. A place on a map needs two, one for each direction.

sentence.da: Breddegraden er en **koordinat** på et kort.
sentence.en: Latitude is a coordinate on a map.

en kop.explanation: "En kop" means "a cup", mostly for hot drinks like coffee and tea. Cold drinks usually go in et glas (a glass): et glas vand (a glass of water).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **kop** kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like a cup of coffee.

en kopi.explanation: "En kopi" means "a copy" of a document, a file or a key.

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge en **kopi** af dit pas.
sentence.en: I need a copy of your passport.

en kopimaskine.explanation: "En kopimaskine" means "a copier", a machine for papers. It is built from kopi (a duplicate) and maskine (machine), which also appears in en vaskemaskine (a washer).

sentence.da: Kan du lave ti kopier på vores **kopimaskine**?
sentence.en: Can you make ten copies on our copier?

en korporal.explanation: "En korporal" means "a corporal", a low rank in the army. It is one of the first ranks a soldier can move up to.

sentence.da: En **korporal** er over en menig og under en sergent.
sentence.en: A corporal is above a private and below a sergeant.

en kosmetolog.explanation: "En kosmetolog" means "a beautician", a trained specialist in skin care and beauty treatments such as facials. A kosmetolog works on the skin, not on the hair.

sentence.da: Min **kosmetolog** giver mig en ansigtsbehandling hver anden måned.
sentence.en: My beautician gives me a facial every other month.

en kost.explanation: "En kost" means "a broom", a brush on a long handle for cleaning the floor. A støvsuger (vacuum cleaner) does the same job with electricity.

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **kost** og fejer køkkenet.
sentence.en: I take a broom and sweep the kitchen.

en kostald.explanation: "En kostald" means "a cowshed", the building where the cows live. It is built from ko (cow) and stald (a shed for farm animals), which can hold any kind: Fårene er i stalden (The sheep are in the shed).

sentence.da: Køerne sover i en stor, varm **kostald**.
sentence.en: The cows sleep in a big, warm cowshed.

en krabbe.explanation: "En krabbe" means "a crab", the sea animal with claws that walks sideways. For crab as food, drop en: Vi spiser krabbe (We eat crab).

sentence.da: En lille **krabbe** går sidelæns over sandet.
sentence.en: A small crab walks sideways over the sand.

en kraft.explanation: "En kraft" means "a force" or "power", the push that makes something move or work, in physics, in nature and in people. For power over others, such as in politics, use magt (power). With all your might is af alle kræfter.

sentence.da: Vinden havde så stor **kraft**, at den væltede træet.
sentence.en: The wind had so much force that it knocked over the tree.

en krage.explanation: "En krage" means "a crow", a common bird with gray and black feathers. It is not the same as en ravn (a raven), which is larger and entirely black.

sentence.da: En **krage** leder ofte efter mad på marker og i byer.
sentence.en: A crow often looks for food in fields and in towns.

en krampe.explanation: "En krampe" means "a cramp", a sudden, painful tightening of a muscle, often in a leg or foot. It goes away when the muscle relaxes.

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **krampe** i læggen, da jeg svømmede.
sentence.en: I got a cramp in my calf when I was swimming.

en kran.explanation: "En kran" means "a crane", the tall machine that lifts heavy things: Kranen løfter stål (The crane lifts steel). The same word also means "a faucet": Luk for kranen (Turn off the faucet).

sentence.da: Den høje **kran** løfter tunge ting.
sentence.en: The tall crane lifts heavy things.

en krans.explanation: "En krans" means "a wreath", a circle made of twigs, leaves or flowers, used for decoration and at funerals. To lay one at a funeral is at lægge en krans (to lay a wreath).

sentence.da: På døren hænger der en **krans** af grene til jul.
sentence.en: On the door hangs a wreath of branches for Christmas.

en kransekage.explanation: "En kransekage" means "a marzipan ring cake", a tall tower of stacked rings. Danes often serve it at New Year and at weddings.

sentence.da: Vi spiser en **kransekage** med marcipan til nytår.
sentence.en: We eat a marzipan ring cake at New Year.

en krave.explanation: "En krave" means "a collar", the part of a shirt or coat that goes around the neck. For a dog's collar, say et halsbånd (a dog collar).

sentence.da: Jakken har en høj **krave**, som holder halsen varm.
sentence.en: The jacket has a high collar that keeps the throat warm.

en krig.explanation: "En krig" means "a war", fighting between countries or groups. The opposite is fred (peace).

sentence.da: Den lange **krig** sluttede i foråret.
sentence.en: The long war ended in the spring.

en krimi.explanation: "En krimi" means "a crime novel" or "a crime show", and it is short for en kriminalroman. It works for books and TV: Vi ser en ny krimi i aften (We are watching a new crime show tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en spændende **krimi** i aften.
sentence.en: I am reading an exciting crime novel tonight.

en kriminalassistent.explanation: "En kriminalassistent" means "a detective sergeant", a police officer who works on solving crimes. It is a title in the Danish police.

sentence.da: En **kriminalassistent** efterforsker sagen og taler med vidnerne.
sentence.en: A detective sergeant investigates the case and talks to the witnesses.

en kriminalbetjent.explanation: "En kriminalbetjent" means "a detective", a police detective who investigates crimes, usually in plain clothes instead of a uniform.

sentence.da: En **kriminalbetjent** undersøger tyverier og andre forbrydelser.
sentence.en: A detective investigates thefts and other offenses.

en krise.explanation: "En krise" means "a crisis", a hard period when things go badly, for a country, a company or a person. Hun er i krise (She is in crisis) can describe a personal collapse too.

sentence.da: Landet er midt i en **krise**, og mange mister deres job.
sentence.en: The country is in the middle of a crisis, and many are losing their jobs.

en kritiker.explanation: "En kritiker" means "a critic", someone who judges and writes about art, books, films or food. It also fits a person who speaks against a plan: kritikere af planen (critics of the plan).

sentence.da: En **kritiker** skriver i avisen om nye film og bøger.
sentence.en: A critic writes in the newspaper about new films and books.

en kro.explanation: "En kro" means "an inn", a place in the countryside where you can eat and often stay overnight.

sentence.da: Vi spiser og sover på en lille **kro** på landet.
sentence.en: We eat and sleep at a small inn in the countryside.

en krog.explanation: "En krog" means "a hook", a bent piece of metal on a wall or at the end of a fishing line. It can also be a cozy nook: en hyggelig krog (a cozy nook).

sentence.da: Hæng jakken på en **krog** ved døren.
sentence.en: Hang the jacket on a hook by the door.

en krokodille.explanation: "En krokodille" means "a crocodile", a large reptile with a long tail that lives in warm rivers and lakes.

sentence.da: En **krokodille** har skarpe tænder.
sentence.en: A crocodile has sharp teeth.

en krone.explanation: "En krone" means "a crown", the money used in Denmark. After a number, you say kroner: tyve kroner means "twenty crowns". The short written form is kr.

sentence.da: En **krone** er hundrede øre.
sentence.en: A krone is a hundred øre.

en kronik.explanation: "En kronik" means "an op-ed", a long piece of writing in a newspaper where someone, often an expert, argues a view. It is longer and more thought through than a short reader comment.

sentence.da: Forskeren skrev en **kronik** i avisen om skolens fremtid.
sentence.en: The researcher wrote an op-ed in the paper about the future of schools.

en kronisk sygdom.explanation: "En kronisk sygdom" means "a chronic illness", an illness that does not go away and has to be managed for a long time, such as asthma. Kronisk alone also fits other things: kronisk træt (constantly tired).

sentence.da: Mange lever et normalt liv med en **kronisk sygdom**.
sentence.en: Many people live a normal life with a chronic illness.

en krop.explanation: "En krop" means "a body". Jeg har ondt i kroppen means "My whole body aches". When one body part hurts, Danish says "the" where English says "my": Jeg har ondt i maven means "My stomach hurts".

sentence.da: Min **krop** er meget træt i dag.
sentence.en: My body is very tired today.

en krukke.explanation: "En krukke" means "a jar", a round container with a wide opening, for food like honey, jam or pickles.

sentence.da: Der står en **krukke** honning i skabet.
sentence.en: There is a jar of honey in the cupboard.

en krydderurt.explanation: "En krydderurt" means "an herb", a plant whose leaves give flavor to food. A krydderi (spice) is usually dried, such as pepper.

sentence.da: Basilikum er en **krydderurt** i mange italienske retter.
sentence.en: Basil is an herb in many Italian dishes.

en krydsogtværs.explanation: "En krydsogtværs" means "a crossword", a game where words cross each other in a grid and you fill them in from hints. The name comes from kryds og tværs (criss-cross), which on its own means in all directions: De løb kryds og tværs (They ran criss-cross).

sentence.da: Hver søndag løser jeg en **krydsogtværs** i avisen.
sentence.en: Every Sunday I solve a crossword in the newspaper.

en krykke.explanation: "En krykke" means "a crutch", a support you place under your arm to walk when a leg or foot is hurt. You normally use two, so you often hear et par krykker (a pair of crutches).

sentence.da: Med et brækket ben støtter man sig til en **krykke**.
sentence.en: With a broken leg you lean on a crutch.

en kuffert.explanation: "En kuffert" means "a suitcase", a large case with a handle for carrying your clothes when you travel. Ud (out) turns at pakke (to pack) into at pakke ud (to unpack), which takes things out of the case.

sentence.da: Jeg har tøj i min **kuffert**.
sentence.en: I have clothes in my suitcase.

en kugle.explanation: "En kugle" means "a ball" or "a bullet", a small solid ball, like a marble: Politiet fandt en kugle i væggen (The police found a bullet in the wall). A football is en bold (a ball).

sentence.da: Hun spiser en **kugle** is i solen.
sentence.en: She is eating a scoop of ice cream in the sun.

en kuglepen.explanation: "En kuglepen" means "a ballpoint pen". It is built from kugle (ball) and pen (pen), because of the tiny ball at the tip.

sentence.da: Jeg skriver et brev med en blå **kuglepen**.
sentence.en: I write a letter with a blue ballpoint pen.

en kujon.explanation: "En kujon" means "a coward", someone who is too scared to face danger or to stand up for something. It is an insult.

sentence.da: Han kaldte mig en **kujon**, fordi jeg ikke turde springe.
sentence.en: He called me a coward because I did not dare to jump.

en kuldebølge.explanation: "En kuldebølge" means "a cold spell", a stretch of unusually cold weather that lasts a while, far below what is normal for the season. Forecasts use it when the cold is serious.

sentence.da: Under en **kuldebølge** er det flere dage i træk under frysepunktet.
sentence.en: During a cold spell it is below freezing for several days in a row.

en kuling.explanation: "En kuling" means "a gale", a very strong wind, often named in weather forecasts for the sea. It is strong, but weaker than en storm (a storm).

sentence.da: Vejrudsigten lover **kuling** ved kysten i aften.
sentence.en: The forecast promises a gale on the coast tonight.

en kultur.explanation: "En kultur" means "a culture", the way of life of a country or group. It also covers art and music: Der er meget kultur i København (There is a lot of culture in Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Jeg vil lære mere om dansk **kultur**.
sentence.en: I want to learn more about Danish culture.

en kulturforskel.explanation: "En kulturforskel" means "a cultural difference", a way that manners or values differ between countries or groups, such as how people greet each other or how direct they are.

sentence.da: Det er en **kulturforskel**, at danskere spiser aftensmad så tidligt.
sentence.en: It is a cultural difference that Danes eat dinner so early.

en kunde.explanation: "En kunde" means "a customer", someone who buys from a shop or uses a service, such as a bank or a hairdresser.

sentence.da: En **kunde** betaler for varerne i butikken.
sentence.en: A customer pays for the goods in the store.

en kunsthistoriker.explanation: "En kunsthistoriker" means "an art historian", a person who has studied the history of art, such as paintings and buildings. Many work at museums or teach at universities.

sentence.da: På museet fortæller en **kunsthistoriker** om malerierne.
sentence.en: At the museum an art historian tells about the paintings.

en kunstner.explanation: "En kunstner" means "an artist", a person who makes art for a living. The word is built from kunst (art). It also covers people who perform, such as a singer: Han er en kendt kunstner, der synger (He is a famous artist who sings).

sentence.da: Den danske **kunstner** maler store billeder.
sentence.en: The Danish artist paints big pictures.

en kunstudstilling.explanation: "En kunstudstilling" means "an art exhibition", an event where artworks are shown to visitors, usually in a museum. The opening evening is called en fernisering (an opening night).

sentence.da: På en **kunstudstilling** kan man se malerier og skulpturer.
sentence.en: At an art exhibition you can see paintings and sculptures.

en kur.explanation: "En kur" means "a cure", a way to make someone well again. It is also a planned course of treatment, and a fixed program such as en slankekur (a weight-loss diet).

sentence.da: Lægerne leder efter en **kur** mod sygdommen.
sentence.en: The doctors are looking for a cure for the disease.

en kurs.explanation: "En kurs" means "a course (direction)" and also "an exchange rate": dollarens kurs (the dollar's rate). A course you attend is et kursus (a course), not en kurs.

sentence.da: Skibet holder **kurs** mod nord, selvom bølgerne er store.
sentence.en: The ship keeps its course north, even though the waves are big.

en kurv.explanation: "En kurv" means "a basket", a container woven from straw or willow, usually with a handle: en kurv med brød (a basket of bread). A bag is a different thing: en pose (a bag).

sentence.da: Æblerne ligger i en **kurv** med hank.
sentence.en: The apples are in a basket with a handle.

en kusine.explanation: "En kusine" means "a female cousin". Danish has two words where English has one: en fætter means "a male cousin".

sentence.da: Min **kusine** er datter af min tante.
sentence.en: My cousin is my aunt's daughter.

en kuvert.explanation: "En kuvert" means "an envelope", the paper cover you put a letter in before you mail it. You write the address on it.

sentence.da: Brevet ligger i en hvid **kuvert** med frimærke.
sentence.en: The letter is in a white envelope with a stamp.

en kvadratmeter.explanation: "En kvadratmeter" means "a square meter", used for the size of rooms and homes: Min lejlighed er 60 kvadratmeter (My apartment is 60 square meters).

sentence.da: Vores stue er cirka tyve **kvadratmeter**.
sentence.en: Our living room is about twenty square meters.

en kvalifikation.explanation: "En kvalifikation" means "a qualification", a skill or training that makes you suited for a job. Job ads list the kvalifikationer (qualifications) they ask for.

sentence.da: Hendes vigtigste **kvalifikation** er ti års erfaring som sygeplejerske.
sentence.en: Her most important qualification is ten years of experience as a nurse.

en kvalitet.explanation: "En kvalitet" means "a quality", how good something is: Det er god kvalitet (It is good quality). It also means a good trait in a person: Ærlighed er en kvalitet (Honesty is a quality).

sentence.da: Jeg vil hellere købe én ting af høj **kvalitet**.
sentence.en: I would rather buy one thing of high quality.

en kvinde.explanation: "En kvinde" means "a woman". Use en pige (a girl) for a girl or a young woman.

sentence.da: En mand og en **kvinde** går forbi.
sentence.en: A man and a woman walk past.

en kvittering.explanation: "En kvittering" means "a receipt". Skal du have kvitteringen? means "Do you want the receipt?". En bon (a till slip) is the short slip that comes out of the cash register, while kvittering is the word for any receipt.

sentence.da: Jeg betalte i butikken og fik en **kvittering**.
sentence.en: I paid in the shop and got a receipt.

en kyst.explanation: "En kyst" means "a coast", the land along the sea: Vi kørte langs kysten (We drove along the coast).

sentence.da: Landet møder havet ved en lang **kyst**.
sentence.en: The land meets the sea at a long coast.

en kystby.explanation: "En kystby" means "a coastal town", a town right by the sea: Skagen er en kystby i Nordjylland (Skagen is a coastal town in North Jutland).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en lille **kystby**, og havet er tæt på.
sentence.en: We live in a small coastal town, and the sea is close.

en kæbe.explanation: "En kæbe" means "a jaw", the bone you chew with. The two parts are overkæbe and underkæbe (upper jaw and lower jaw).

sentence.da: Vores tænder sidder fast i en **kæbe**.
sentence.en: Our teeth are fixed in a jaw.

en kæde.explanation: "En kæde" means "a chain", like on a bike or around the neck. It can also be a group of shops: en kæde af butikker (a chain of stores).

sentence.da: Min cykel har en rusten **kæde**.
sentence.en: My bike has a rusty chain.

en kælder.explanation: "En kælder" means "a basement" or "a cellar", the room under a house, below the ground floor. It is often used for storage: Vi opbevarer cyklerne i kælderen (We keep the bikes in the basement).

sentence.da: Under huset ligger en mørk **kælder**.
sentence.en: Under the house there is a dark basement.

en kæledyrsforsikring.explanation: "En kæledyrsforsikring" means "a pet insurance policy", a monthly payment that covers treatment if your dog or cat gets sick or hurt. It usually covers only part of the cost.

sentence.da: Hundens operation var dyr, men vores **kæledyrsforsikring** betalte det meste.
sentence.en: The dog's operation was expensive, but our pet insurance paid most of it.

en kæmpe.explanation: "En kæmpe" means "a giant", a very big person in stories: Kæmpen er tre meter høj (The giant is three meters tall). Before another word, kæmpe means "huge": en kæmpe fejl (a huge mistake).

sentence.da: I eventyret møder drengen en **kæmpe**.
sentence.en: In the fairy tale, the boy meets a giant.

en kæreste.explanation: "En kæreste" means "a partner" in the romantic sense: a boyfriend or girlfriend you are not necessarily married to. It comes from kær (dear).

sentence.da: Jeg bor sammen med min **kæreste**.
sentence.en: I live together with my partner.

en kø.explanation: "En kø" means "a queue", a line of people or cars waiting: Der er kø i supermarkedet (There is a line in the supermarket). It also means a traffic jam: Der er kø på motorvejen (There is a traffic jam on the highway).

sentence.da: Der er en lang **kø** ved kassen.
sentence.en: There is a long line at the checkout.

en københavner.explanation: "En københavner" means "a Copenhagener", a person who lives in or comes from Copenhagen, the capital. Other cities have their own word, for example en aarhusianer (a person from Aarhus).

sentence.da: Som **københavner** tager jeg ofte cyklen på arbejde.
sentence.en: As a Copenhagener I often take the bike to work.

en købmand.explanation: "En købmand" means "a grocer" or "a shopkeeper". Many Danes still say købmanden for the small food shop in their neighborhood: Jeg køber brød hos købmanden (I buy bread at the grocer's).

sentence.da: Vores **købmand** har altid friske grøntsager.
sentence.en: Our grocer always has fresh vegetables.

en kødbolle.explanation: "En kødbolle" means "a meatball", a small round ball of ground meat, often cooked in soup or in curry sauce (boller i karry, meatballs in curry).

sentence.da: Rul det hakkede kød til en **kødbolle** og steg den.
sentence.en: Roll the minced meat into a meatball and fry it.

en kødspiser.explanation: "En kødspiser" means "a meat eater", a person who eats meat, in contrast to a vegetar (vegetarian). It is used when the contrast matters, for example when planning a menu: Er du kødspiser? (Are you a meat eater?).

sentence.da: Min bror er **kødspiser**, men min søster spiser kun grøntsager.
sentence.en: My brother is a meat eater, but my sister only eats vegetables.

en køjeseng.explanation: "En køjeseng" means "a bunk bed", two beds built one above the other. It is built from køje (bunk) and seng (bed), and a ladder leads up to the top one.

sentence.da: To børn sover over hinanden i en **køjeseng**.
sentence.en: Two children sleep above each other in a bunk bed.

en køkkenchef.explanation: "En køkkenchef" means "a head chef", the person in charge of a restaurant kitchen.

sentence.da: Som **køkkenchef** planlægger hun menuen og leder alle kokkene.
sentence.en: As head chef she plans the menu and leads all the cooks.

en køkkenhave.explanation: "En køkkenhave" means "a vegetable garden", a part of a yard where you grow vegetables and herbs for your own kitchen. A garden only for looks is called en prydhave (an ornamental garden).

sentence.da: I vores **køkkenhave** gror der gulerødder, kartofler og salat.
sentence.en: In our vegetable garden carrots, potatoes and lettuce grow.

en køkkenrulle.explanation: "En køkkenrulle" means "a roll of paper towels", used for wiping up spills in the kitchen.

sentence.da: Jeg har spildt mælk og skal bruge en **køkkenrulle**.
sentence.en: I have spilled milk and need a roll of paper towels.

en køkkenvægt.explanation: "En køkkenvægt" means "a kitchen scale", used to weigh ingredients exactly when you bake. It is built from køkken (kitchen) and vægt (scale).

sentence.da: Jeg vejer melet på en **køkkenvægt**.
sentence.en: I weigh the flour on a kitchen scale.

en kørelærer.explanation: "En kørelærer" means "a driving instructor", the person who teaches you to drive. It is built from at køre (to drive) and en lærer (a teacher). The verb at køre also covers riding as a passenger: Jeg kører med bussen (I go by bus).

sentence.da: Min **kørelærer** sidder ved siden af mig i bilen.
sentence.en: My driving instructor sits next to me in the car.

en køreplan.explanation: "En køreplan" means "a timetable" for buses and trains. It shows when each one leaves.

sentence.da: Jeg kigger i en **køreplan**, fordi jeg tager toget.
sentence.en: I look in a timetable because I am taking the train.

en køreprøve.explanation: "En køreprøve" means "a driving test": Jeg skal til køreprøve på mandag (I have my driving test on Monday). It has two parts, a theory test and a driving part.

sentence.da: Hun bestod sin **køreprøve** i går.
sentence.en: She passed her driving test yesterday.

en køreskole.explanation: "En køreskole" means "a driving school", where you learn to drive: Jeg går på køreskole (I am taking driving lessons). After the lessons you take your køreprøve (driving test).

sentence.da: Min søster går på **køreskole** og lærer at køre.
sentence.en: My sister goes to driving school and learns to drive.

en kørestol.explanation: "En kørestol" means "a wheelchair", a chair with wheels for someone who cannot walk, or cannot walk far. You say that someone sits in one: Han sidder i kørestol (He uses a wheelchair).

sentence.da: Hun kan ikke gå, så hun bruger en **kørestol**.
sentence.en: She cannot walk, so she uses a wheelchair.

en kørsel.explanation: "En kørsel" means "a drive" or "a trip" in a vehicle. It comes from at køre (to drive).

sentence.da: En **kørsel** til lufthavnen tager en time.
sentence.en: A drive to the airport takes an hour.

et kaffebord.explanation: "Et kaffebord" means "a coffee table (with cake)", a gathering where visitors are served coffee and cake, for example after a christening, a confirmation or a funeral. It is not a piece of furniture. The table in a living room is et sofabord.

sentence.da: Efter dåben var der **kaffebord** med lagkage til alle gæsterne.
sentence.en: After the christening, there was coffee and cake for all the guests.

et kaffefilter.explanation: "Et kaffefilter" means "a coffee filter", the paper that catches the coffee grounds when you brew coffee.

sentence.da: Kaffemaskinen virker ikke uden et **kaffefilter**.
sentence.en: The coffee machine does not work without a coffee filter.

et kalenderlys.explanation: "Et kalenderlys" means "an Advent calendar candle", a candle marked with the numbers 1 to 24. Each day in December, you light it and let it burn down to that day's number.

sentence.da: Et **kalenderlys** hjælper børnene med at tælle dagene til jul.
sentence.en: A calendar candle helps the children count the days until Christmas.

et kamera.explanation: "Et kamera" means "a camera", including the one in your phone.

sentence.da: Min telefon har et rigtig godt **kamera**.
sentence.en: My phone has a really good camera.

et kapitel.explanation: "Et kapitel" means "a chapter" of a book. It also works for a period of life: Det var et vigtigt kapitel i hans liv (It was an important chapter in his life).

sentence.da: Jeg læser et **kapitel** hver aften.
sentence.en: I read a chapter every evening.

et karaktergennemsnit.explanation: "Et karaktergennemsnit" means "a grade point average", the average of all your grades. In Denmark, grades run from -3 to 12, and the average often decides whether you get into a university program.

sentence.da: Med et højt **karaktergennemsnit** kan man komme ind på de fleste uddannelser.
sentence.en: With a high grade point average, you can get into most programs.

et kartotekskort.explanation: "Et kartotekskort" means "an index card", a small stiff card for writing one fact or a few words on. Students often use them for studying, with a question on one side and the answer on the other.

sentence.da: Jeg skriver ordet på et **kartotekskort** og lærer det udenad.
sentence.en: I write the word on an index card and learn it by heart.

et kasino.explanation: "Et kasino" means "a casino", a place where people play games for money. For a slot machine, say en spillemaskine (a slot machine).

sentence.da: Vi spiller kort med penge på et **kasino**.
sentence.en: We play cards for money at a casino.

et katalog.explanation: "Et katalog" means "a catalog", a booklet or website that lists products and prices.

sentence.da: Jeg bladrer i et **katalog** og finder en ny jakke.
sentence.en: I flip through a catalog and find a new jacket.

et kemikalie.explanation: "Et kemikalie" means "a chemical", a material used or made in industry, farming or research. It is often used in the plural, with a warning: Pas på kemikalier! (Be careful with chemicals!)

sentence.da: Man skal bruge handsker, når man arbejder med et **kemikalie**.
sentence.en: You must wear gloves when you work with a chemical.

et kendetegn.explanation: "Et kendetegn" means "a characteristic", a typical feature that lets you recognize a person, an animal or a thing. It is built from at kende (to recognize) and et tegn (a sign), so it is literally "a sign you know it by".

sentence.da: Sorte og hvide striber er et **kendetegn** ved zebraen.
sentence.en: Black and white stripes are a characteristic of the zebra.

et kilo.explanation: "Et kilo" means "a kilo", short for et kilogram (a kilogram).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have et **kilo** æbler.
sentence.en: I would like a kilo of apples.

et kirsebær.explanation: "Et kirsebær" means "a cherry". The word ends in bær (berry), like et jordbær (a strawberry).

sentence.da: Jeg putter et **kirsebær** på kagen.
sentence.en: I put a cherry on the cake.

et klasseværelse.explanation: "Et klasseværelse" means "a classroom". It is built from klasse (class) and værelse (room). Klasse also means a school year: Hun går i tredje klasse (She is in third grade).

sentence.da: Eleverne sidder i et lyst **klasseværelse**.
sentence.en: The students sit in a bright classroom.

et klaver.explanation: "Et klaver" means "a piano". Danish leaves out the word the when you play it: at spille klaver (to play the piano). Klaver is the normal word, though et piano (a piano) is also understood.

sentence.da: Hun spiller **klaver** hjemme.
sentence.en: She plays the piano at home.

et klima.explanation: "Et klima" means "a climate", the usual weather in a place over many years. Do not mix it up with et vejr (weather), which is just today's weather.

sentence.da: Danmark har et mildt **klima**, men det regner meget.
sentence.en: Denmark has a mild climate, but it rains a lot.

et klimaks.explanation: "Et klimaks" means "a climax", the most exciting moment in a story, a film or a piece of music, when everything has built up to its peak. It can also be the peak of an event or a development.

sentence.da: Bogens **klimaks** er, når helten endelig møder skurken.
sentence.en: The climax of the book is when the hero finally meets the villain.

et klip.explanation: "Et klip" means "a cut / clip", a short piece taken out of something bigger, such as a scene from a film or a video. It can also be a single quick snip: Ét klip, og snoren var skåret over (One snip, and the string was cut).

sentence.da: Jeg sendte min veninde et sjovt **klip** fra filmen.
sentence.en: I sent my friend a funny clip from the movie.

et klippekort.explanation: "Et klippekort" means "a punch card", a card with a set number of rides or visits for the bus, a swimming pool or a gym: Klippekortet har tre klip tilbage (The punch card has three punches left).

sentence.da: Jeg har et **klippekort** med ti ture.
sentence.en: I have a punch card with ten rides.

et kloster.explanation: "Et kloster" means "a monastery / convent", a place where people live a religious life together, set apart from ordinary society. Danish uses the same word for the men's and the women's version.

sentence.da: Munke og nonner bor sammen i et **kloster** og beder hver dag.
sentence.en: Monks and nuns live together in a monastery and pray every day.

et klædeskab.explanation: "Et klædeskab" means "a wardrobe". It is built from klæder (clothes) and skab (cupboard). Skab also ends et køleskab (a fridge).

sentence.da: Tøjet hænger i et **klædeskab** i soveværelset.
sentence.en: The clothes hang in a wardrobe in the bedroom.

et knep.explanation: "Et knep" means "a trick", a clever way of doing something more easily, a handy technique. A magic trick is something else, et tryllenummer.

sentence.da: Hun kender et **knep** til at få tøjet tørt hurtigere.
sentence.en: She knows a trick for getting the clothes dry faster.

et knus.explanation: "Et knus" means "a hug". It is often written at the end of messages to friends: Knus fra Maria (Hugs from Maria).

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig et stort **knus**.
sentence.en: I am sending you a big hug.

et knæ.explanation: "Et knæ" means "a knee". The k is pronounced, so say k-næ.

sentence.da: Hun faldt og slog sit **knæ**.
sentence.en: She fell and hurt her knee.

et kodeord.explanation: "Et kodeord" means "a password". It is literally a code word, from en kode (a code) and et ord (a word).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge **kodeord** for at logge ind.
sentence.en: You need a password to log in.

et kollegieværelse.explanation: "Et kollegieværelse" means "a dorm room", a student's own room in a kollegium (a student residence). It is usually a single room, and the kitchen is often shared with the other students.

sentence.da: Mit **kollegieværelse** er lille, og der står kun en seng og et skrivebord.
sentence.en: My dorm room is small, and there is only a bed and a desk.

et kollegium.explanation: "Et kollegium" means "a student dormitory": a building where students have their own rooms and often share a kitchen. In Danish you live på (at) it, without et: Han bor på kollegium (He lives in a dorm).

sentence.da: Jeg flytter ind på **kollegium** i september.
sentence.en: I am moving into a dorm in September.

et kolon.explanation: "Et kolon" means "a colon", the punctuation mark : used before a list or an explanation: Jeg skal bruge tre ting: mel, æg og sukker (I need three things: flour, eggs and sugar).

sentence.da: Et **kolon** består af to prikker over hinanden.
sentence.en: A colon is made of two dots on top of each other.

et koma.explanation: "Et koma" means "a coma", a deep, sleep-like state from which a person cannot be woken, caused by serious illness or an accident. Hun lå i koma i to uger (She was in a coma for two weeks). Watch the spelling: one m, not two.

sentence.da: Lægerne lagde patienten i kunstigt **koma**, så kroppen kunne hele.
sentence.en: The doctors put the patient in an induced coma so the body could heal.

et komfur.explanation: "Et komfur" means "a stove", the kitchen appliance with burners where you cook food.

sentence.da: Gryden med suppen står på et **komfur**.
sentence.en: The pot of soup is on a stove.

et komma.explanation: "Et komma" means "a comma", the punctuation mark , . Danish uses it more than English does, for example before at (that): Jeg tror, at det er sandt (I think that it is true). Watch the spelling: two m, not one.

sentence.da: Der skal stå et **komma** foran ordet men.
sentence.en: There must be a comma in front of the word men (but).

et kommunalvalg.explanation: "Et kommunalvalg" means "a local election", an election where people choose who runs their town, including schools, care for older people and local roads. Foreign residents often have the right to take part too.

sentence.da: Hvert fjerde år er der et **kommunalvalg**, hvor man vælger byrådet.
sentence.en: Every four years there is a local election, where you choose the city council.

et kompagni.explanation: "Et kompagni" means "a company (military or business)", mostly a unit of soldiers in the army. In old business names it is the same as English Co.: Hansen & Kompagni (Hansen & Co.).

sentence.da: Et **kompagni** består af flere mindre grupper af soldater.
sentence.en: A company consists of several smaller groups of soldiers.

et kompas.explanation: "Et kompas" means "a compass", the tool with a needle that points north.

sentence.da: Vi bruger et **kompas** til at finde vej.
sentence.en: We use a compass to find our way.

et kompliment.explanation: "Et kompliment" means "a compliment", a kind thing you say about someone.

sentence.da: Hun gav mig et **kompliment** for min kjole.
sentence.en: She gave me a compliment on my dress.

et kompromis.explanation: "Et kompromis" means "a compromise", a solution where each side gives up part of what it wanted. The usual phrase is at indgå et kompromis (to reach a compromise).

sentence.da: Vi kunne ikke blive enige, så vi fandt et **kompromis**.
sentence.en: We could not agree, so we found a compromise.

et koncerthus.explanation: "Et koncerthus" means "a concert hall", a building made for concerts, with seats for a big audience and a platform for the musicians. One example is Koncerthuset in Copenhagen.

sentence.da: Orkestret spiller for tusind tilhørere i et stort **koncerthus**.
sentence.en: The orchestra plays for a thousand listeners in a big concert hall.

et konditori.explanation: "Et konditori" means "a pastry shop / café", a traditional shop where cakes and fine baked sweets are made and sold, often with tables where you can sit down with coffee.

sentence.da: På et **konditori** kan man sidde ned og spise kage med kaffe.
sentence.en: At a pastry shop, you can sit down and eat cake with coffee.

et kondom.explanation: "Et kondom" means "a condom", a thin rubber cover used during sex. It is sold in most supermarkets.

sentence.da: Et **kondom** beskytter både mod graviditet og mod seksuelt overførte sygdomme.
sentence.en: A condom protects against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases.

et kongehus.explanation: "Et kongehus" means "a royal family", the ruling family of a country. It is literally a king house, like the House of Windsor in English.

sentence.da: Et **kongehus** er den familie, som har en konge eller en dronning.
sentence.en: A royal family is the family that has a king or a queen.

et kongerige.explanation: "Et kongerige" means "a kingdom", a country ruled by a king or a queen. Denmark's official name is Kongeriget Danmark (the Kingdom of Denmark), which also includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

sentence.da: Danmark er et **kongerige**, fordi landet har en konge.
sentence.en: Denmark is a kingdom because the country has a king.

et kongresmedlem.explanation: "Et kongresmedlem" means "a member of Congress", a person elected to the US lawmaking body in Washington. It is built from en kongres (a congress) and et medlem (a member).

sentence.da: Et **kongresmedlem** stemmer om nye love i Washington.
sentence.en: A member of Congress votes on new laws in Washington.

et konsulat.explanation: "Et konsulat" means "a consulate", an office of one country in a city of another country, which helps its own citizens who live or travel there.

sentence.da: Hvis du mister dit pas i udlandet, kan du få hjælp på et **konsulat**.
sentence.en: If you lose your passport abroad, you can get help at a consulate.

et kontantbeløb.explanation: "Et kontantbeløb" means "a cash amount", a sum paid in bills and coins instead of by card. It is the word used in rules and contracts, for example for a payment that must be made in cash. In everyday speech Danes just say kontanter (cash).

sentence.da: Han betalte et **kontantbeløb** i stedet for at bruge kort.
sentence.en: He paid a cash amount instead of using a card.

et kontinent.explanation: "Et kontinent" means "a continent", one of the very large parts of the Earth, such as Europa (Europe) or Asien (Asia).

sentence.da: Afrika er et **kontinent** med mange lande.
sentence.en: Africa is a continent with many countries.

et kontor.explanation: "Et kontor" means "an office". Et postkontor (a post office) is built on the same word.

sentence.da: Hun arbejder ved en computer på et **kontor**.
sentence.en: She works at a computer in an office.

et kontorhus.explanation: "Et kontorhus" means "an office building", a building where companies have their offices. It is built from et kontor (an office) and et hus (a house).

sentence.da: Mange firmaer har kontorer i et **kontorhus**.
sentence.en: Many companies have offices in an office building.

et kor.explanation: "Et kor" means "a choir", a group of people who sing together. The phrase i kor means "in unison": De råbte i kor (They shouted together).

sentence.da: Hun synger i et **kor** hver tirsdag.
sentence.en: She sings in a choir every Tuesday.

et kors.explanation: "Et kors" means "a cross", the shape of two lines that cross each other, and the Christian symbol. For an X mark on a form, use et kryds (a check or X mark) instead.

sentence.da: Danmarks flag har et hvidt **kors** på rød baggrund.
sentence.en: The flag of Denmark has a white cross on a red background.

et kort.explanation: "Et kort" means both "a map" and "a card", so the context tells you which: et kort over Danmark (a map of Denmark) or et kreditkort (a credit card). On its own, kort also means "short": en kort tur (a short trip).

sentence.da: Jeg kigger på et **kort** over byen.
sentence.en: I look at a map of the town.

et kortspil.explanation: "Et kortspil" means "a card game". It is built from et kort (a card) and et spil (a game). It can also mean a pack of cards: Hvor er kortspillet? (Where is the deck?).

sentence.da: Poker er et populært **kortspil**.
sentence.en: Poker is a popular card game.

et kosttilskud.explanation: "Et kosttilskud" means "a dietary supplement", built from kost (diet) and tilskud (addition). It is something you take in addition to your meals to get extra nutrients.

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **kosttilskud** med D-vitamin hver dag.
sentence.en: I take a supplement with vitamin D every day.

et kostume.explanation: "Et kostume" means "a costume", clothes you wear to look like someone else.

sentence.da: Børn har **kostume** på til fastelavn.
sentence.en: Children wear costumes at carnival.

et kostumebal.explanation: "Et kostumebal" means "a costume party", a party where all the guests wear costumes. Bal alone means a ball, a dance party.

sentence.da: Til et **kostumebal** er alle klædt ud som figurer eller dyr.
sentence.en: At a costume party, everyone is dressed up as characters or animals.

et kraftværk.explanation: "Et kraftværk" means "a power plant", a large facility that produces electricity. Værk (work) in a name often means a place where something is produced.

sentence.da: Et **kraftværk** laver strøm til tusindvis af hjem.
sentence.en: A power plant makes electricity for thousands of homes.

et kram.explanation: "Et kram" means "a hug". To hug someone, use at kramme (to hug): Hun krammer sin søn (She hugs her son).

sentence.da: Min datter gav mig et stort **kram**.
sentence.en: My daughter gave me a big hug.

et kranie.explanation: "Et kranie" means "a skull", the hard bones of the head that protect the brain.

sentence.da: Hjernen er beskyttet af et hårdt **kranie**.
sentence.en: The brain is protected by a hard skull.

et krat.explanation: "Et krat" means "a thicket", a dense patch of small trees and shrubs that is hard to walk through. It is much smaller than a forest.

sentence.da: Rådyret gemmer sig i et tæt **krat** ved søen.
sentence.en: The roe deer hides in a dense thicket by the lake.

et krav.explanation: "Et krav" means "a requirement", something that must be met, and also "a demand". A common pattern is at stille krav (to make demands).

sentence.da: Der er et **krav** om, at man skal være atten år.
sentence.en: There is a requirement that you must be eighteen years old.

et kreditkort.explanation: "Et kreditkort" means "a credit card". It is built from kredit (credit) and kort (card). Kort also means a map: Har du et kort over byen? (Do you have a map of the city?)

sentence.da: Kan jeg betale med **kreditkort** her?
sentence.en: Can I pay with a credit card here?

et kredsløb.explanation: "Et kredsløb" means "a circuit", a path that goes round and ends where it began, and also "circulation" in the body. It is also the path of a satellite around the Earth: en satellits kredsløb (a satellite's orbit).

sentence.da: Blodets **kredsløb** går rundt i hele kroppen.
sentence.en: The circulation of the blood goes around the whole body.

et kriterium.explanation: "Et kriterium" means "a criterion", a standard used to judge or choose something. It is common in rules and applications: kriterier for optagelse (criteria for admission).

sentence.da: Prisen er det vigtigste **kriterium**, når vi vælger en bil.
sentence.en: The price is the most important criterion when we choose a car.

et kronblad.explanation: "Et kronblad" means "a petal", one of the colored parts of a flower. All the petals together are called en krone (a corolla, literally a crown).

sentence.da: Hvert **kronblad** på solsikken er gult.
sentence.en: Each petal on the sunflower is yellow.

et krus.explanation: "Et krus" means "a mug", a big cup with a handle. For a normal cup, say en kop (a cup).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker min kaffe af et stort **krus**.
sentence.en: I drink my coffee from a big mug.

et krydderi.explanation: "Et krydderi" means "a spice" or seasoning. A fresh herb is en krydderurt (a herb).

sentence.da: Man bruger **krydderi** for at give mad smag.
sentence.en: You use spice to give food flavor.

et kryds.explanation: "Et kryds" means "an intersection" where two roads meet. It also means a cross mark: sæt et kryds (put an X).

sentence.da: Drej til venstre i det næste **kryds**.
sentence.en: Turn left at the next intersection.

et krydstogt.explanation: "Et krydstogt" means "a cruise", a vacation on a big ship that visits several places.

sentence.da: På et **krydstogt** bor man på et stort skib.
sentence.en: On a cruise you live on a big ship.

et kunstværk.explanation: "Et kunstværk" means "a work of art", something made to be looked at or experienced, such as a painting or a sculpture.

sentence.da: Maleriet er et **kunstværk**, som mange mennesker vil se.
sentence.en: The painting is a work of art that many people want to see.

et kup.explanation: "Et kup" means "a coup" and "a heist": a sudden, planned action that surprises everyone. It can be a takeover of power, a daring robbery or a lucky bargain: Jeg gjorde et kup på markedet (I got a bargain at the market).

sentence.da: Hæren tog magten i landet ved et **kup**.
sentence.en: The army took power in the country in a coup.

et kursus.explanation: "Et kursus" means "a course", a set of classes on one topic, often for adults. To attend one, say gå på kursus (go on a course): Hun går på kursus i aften (She is at a course tonight).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **kursus** i spansk i foråret.
sentence.en: I am taking a Spanish course in the spring.

et kvadrat.explanation: "Et kvadrat" means "a square", the shape with four equal sides. A town square is not this word; that is et torv (a town square).

sentence.da: Hun tegner et **kvadrat** med fire lige sider.
sentence.en: She draws a square with four equal sides.

et kvartal.explanation: "Et kvartal" means "a quarter" of a year, three months, as used in company reports. It also means a city block: et roligt kvartal (a quiet neighborhood). Do not mix it up with et kvarter (a quarter of an hour).

sentence.da: Firmaet tjente flere penge i første **kvartal** i år end sidste år.
sentence.en: The company earned more money in the first quarter this year than last year.

et kvarter.explanation: "Et kvarter" means "a neighborhood", a part of a town. The same word also means "quarter of an hour": Vi ses om et kvarter (See you in 15 minutes).

sentence.da: Vi bor i et rart **kvarter** tæt på centrum.
sentence.en: We live in a nice neighborhood close to the center.

et kys.explanation: "Et kys" means "a kiss". To kiss someone, use at kysse (to kiss): Han kysser hende (He kisses her).

sentence.da: Hun gav ham et **kys** på kinden.
sentence.en: She gave him a kiss on the cheek.

et kæledyr.explanation: "Et kæledyr" means "a pet", an animal you keep at home for company, such as a dog or cat. It is made of at kæle (to cuddle) and et dyr (an animal).

sentence.da: Vi har en hund som **kæledyr**.
sentence.en: We have a dog as a pet.

et kælenavn.explanation: "Et kælenavn" means "a nickname", a loving name that family and close friends use: Min mor kalder mig skat (My mom calls me sweetheart). It is built from at kæle (to cuddle) and navn (name).

sentence.da: Han bruger et **kælenavn** i stedet for hendes rigtige navn.
sentence.en: He uses a nickname instead of her real name.

et kærestepar.explanation: "Et kærestepar" means "a couple (dating)", two people in a relationship who are not married. For married people, say et ægtepar (a married couple).

sentence.da: Det unge **kærestepar** holder hinanden i hånden.
sentence.en: The young couple is holding hands.

et kærlighedsbrev.explanation: "Et kærlighedsbrev" means "a love letter", a letter in which you tell someone you love them. It is built from kærlighed (love) and brev (letter). Brev also begins en brevkasse (a mailbox).

sentence.da: Hans **kærlighedsbrev** sagde: Jeg elsker dig.
sentence.en: His love letter said: I love you.

et kærlighedsforhold.explanation: "Et kærlighedsforhold" means "a romantic relationship", a relationship built on love between two people. Forhold alone also means "relationship" in other settings: et godt forhold til min chef (a good relationship with my boss).

sentence.da: Et **kærlighedsforhold** er, når to mennesker elsker hinanden og er sammen.
sentence.en: A romantic relationship is when two people love each other and are together.

et køkken.explanation: "Et køkken" means "a kitchen", the room where you cook food. It can also mean a style of cooking: det danske køkken means "Danish cuisine".

sentence.da: Jeg laver aftensmad i et lille **køkken**.
sentence.en: I make dinner in a small kitchen.

et køkkenbord.explanation: "Et køkkenbord" means "a kitchen table", where a family eats in the kitchen, and also "a kitchen counter", the work surface where you prepare food: Jeg skærer brød på køkkenbordet (I cut bread on the kitchen counter).

sentence.da: Vi spiser morgenmad ved vores **køkkenbord**.
sentence.en: We eat breakfast at our kitchen table.

et køkkenur.explanation: "Et køkkenur" means "a kitchen timer", the small clock that counts down while you cook. It is built from køkken (kitchen) and ur (clock). Ur also means a watch: Min far har et nyt ur (My dad has a new watch).

sentence.da: Jeg stillede et **køkkenur** på tyve minutter.
sentence.en: I set a kitchen timer for twenty minutes.

et køleskab.explanation: "Et køleskab" means "a fridge". It is made of køle (cool) and et skab (a cupboard), so it is literally a cooling cupboard. Skab also ends et klædeskab (a wardrobe).

sentence.da: Mælken står i et **køleskab**.
sentence.en: The milk is in the fridge.

et køn.explanation: "Et køn" means "a gender" and "a sex", being male or female.

sentence.da: På formularen skal du skrive dit **køn** og din alder.
sentence.en: On the form you must write your gender and your age.

et kønummer.explanation: "Et kønummer" means "a queue number", a small slip with a number that you take at a pharmacy or an office and then wait until your number is called.

sentence.da: Tag et **kønummer** og vent, til din tur kommer.
sentence.en: Take a queue number and wait until your turn comes.

et kørekort.explanation: "Et kørekort" means "a driver's license". The usual verb is at tage (to take): Jeg tager kørekort i år (I am getting my license this year).

sentence.da: Jeg må ikke køre bil uden **kørekort**.
sentence.en: I am not allowed to drive a car without a license.

et køretøj.explanation: "Et køretøj" means "a vehicle", anything that drives on the road, like a car, a truck or a motorcycle. It is built from køre (to drive) and tøj (gear).

sentence.da: En lastbil er et stort **køretøj**.
sentence.en: A truck is a big vehicle.

kaffe.explanation: "Kaffe" means "coffee". To order it, you can say en kaffe, tak (a coffee, please) or just kaffe, tak. To invite someone, say Skal vi have en kop kaffe? (Shall we have a cup of coffee?).

sentence.da: **Kaffe** laves af kaffebønner og varmt vand.
sentence.en: Coffee is made from coffee beans and hot water.

kajak.explanation: "Kajak" means "kayaking" and also "a kayak", the small boat: Vi sejler i kajak på søen (We go kayaking on the lake). With a color or size, add en: en rød kajak (a red kayak).

sentence.da: En **kajak** er en smal båd, og man sidder lavt i den.
sentence.en: A kayak is a narrow boat, and you sit low in it.

kakao.explanation: "Kakao" means "cocoa" or "hot chocolate", the drink as well as the powder.

sentence.da: Man laver **kakao** af mælk og kakaopulver.
sentence.en: You make cocoa from milk and cocoa powder.

kakaomælk.explanation: "Kakaomælk" means "chocolate milk", built from kakao (cocoa) and mælk (milk). Hot chocolate is varm kakao (hot cocoa).

sentence.da: **Kakaomælk** er mælk med kakao i, og børn elsker den.
sentence.en: Chocolate milk is milk with cocoa in it, and children love it.

kan du gentage det?.explanation: "Kan du gentage det?" means "Can you repeat that?" and is a polite way to ask when you did not catch what someone said. Add tak (please) to be extra polite: Kan du gentage det, tak?

sentence.da: Undskyld, **kan du gentage det**?
sentence.en: Sorry, can you repeat that?

kan jeg betale med kort?.explanation: "Kan jeg betale med kort?" means "can I pay by card?". Med means "with" and kort means "card". For cash, swap med kort for kontant (in cash): Kan jeg betale kontant? (Can I pay in cash?).

sentence.da: Hej, **kan jeg betale med kort**?
sentence.en: Hi, can I pay by card?

kan jeg købe ...?.explanation: "Kan jeg købe ...?" means "can I buy ...?". Kan jeg means "can I", and you put what you want in place of the dots. Danes also often say jeg vil gerne have... (I would like...).

sentence.da: Undskyld, **kan jeg købe** en kop kaffe?
sentence.en: Excuse me, can I buy a cup of coffee?

kanel.explanation: "Kanel" means "cinnamon", the sweet brown spice used in baking.

sentence.da: Jeg putter **kanel** i min grød.
sentence.en: I put cinnamon in my porridge.

kaos.explanation: "Kaos" means "chaos". Det rene kaos (Pure chaos) is a common way to say that things are completely out of control.

sentence.da: Når alle råber, bliver det hurtigt til **kaos**.
sentence.en: When everyone shouts, it quickly turns into chaos.

karantæne.explanation: "En karantæne" means "a quarantine", a period when you stay away from others so that an illness does not spread. It can apply to people, and also to animals or goods that must wait before entering a country.

sentence.da: Efter rejsen skal man være i **karantæne** i ti dage.
sentence.en: After the trip, you must be in quarantine for ten days.

karry.explanation: "Karry" means "curry", a yellow spice mix with a warm, sharp taste. You buy it as a powder, karrypulver (curry powder).

sentence.da: **Karry** er et gult krydderi til indisk mad.
sentence.en: Curry is a yellow spice for Indian food.

kartofler.explanation: "Kartofler" means "potatoes". Say how they are cooked by putting a word in front, as in kogte kartofler (boiled potatoes) or stegte kartofler (fried potatoes).

sentence.da: Pommes frites er lavet af **kartofler**.
sentence.en: French fries are made of potatoes.

kattemad.explanation: "Kattemad" means "cat food". It is built from kat (cat) and mad (food), and mad also builds morgenmad (breakfast) and aftensmad (dinner).

sentence.da: **Kattemad** er mad til katte, ikke til mennesker.
sentence.en: Cat food is food for cats, not for people.

ked af.explanation: "Ked af" means "sorry" or "sad". Jeg er ked af det can mean either "I am sorry" or "I am sad", and the situation tells you which. Undskyld (sorry, excuse me) is the quick word for small things, such as bumping into someone.

forms.en: I am sorry about it / I am sad about it.

forms.da: Jeg er ked af, at jeg kom for sent.
forms.en: I am sorry that I came too late.

sentence.da: Hun græder og er **ked af** det.
sentence.en: She is crying and she is sad.

ked af det.explanation: "Ked af det" means "sad" or "upset". It is used after er (am, is, are). Jeg er ked af det can also mean "I am sorry", so the situation tells you which.

sentence.da: Barnet græder og er **ked af det**.
sentence.en: The child is crying and is sad.

kedelig.explanation: "Kedelig" means "boring", for things and for people. It can also mean "unfortunate": Det er kedeligt often means "That is too bad". If you are bored yourself, say Jeg keder mig (I am bored).

sentence.da: Filmen er **kedelig**, og jeg gaber.
sentence.en: The film is boring, and I am yawning.

kedsomhed.explanation: "En kedsomhed" means "boredom", the feeling of having nothing interesting to do. It is the feeling itself, while kedelig (boring) describes what causes it.

sentence.da: Når regnen holder os inde, melder **kedsomhed** sig hurtigt.
sentence.en: When the rain keeps us inside, boredom soon shows up.

kemi.explanation: "Kemi" means "chemistry", the study of substances and how they change. For a school class, you leave out en: Vi har kemi på torsdag (We have chemistry on Thursday).

sentence.da: I **kemi** laver vi forsøg i laboratoriet.
sentence.en: In chemistry we do experiments in the lab.

kemisk.explanation: "Kemisk" means "chemical" and describes anything to do with substances and how they react. It also appears in kemisk rensning (dry cleaning), which is cleaning with chemicals instead of water.

sentence.da: Rust er en **kemisk** reaktion mellem jern og ilt.
sentence.en: Rust is a chemical reaction between iron and oxygen.

kendskab.explanation: "Et kendskab" means "knowledge" in the sense of being familiar with a person, a place or a subject, and it is usually followed by til: godt kendskab til byen (good knowledge of the city). Facts you have learned and studied are called viden.

sentence.da: Hun har godt **kendskab** til dansk historie.
sentence.en: She has good knowledge of Danish history.

kendt.explanation: "Kendt" means "known" and also "famous": Hun er kendt for sin musik (She is known for her music). Han er en kendt skuespiller (He is a famous actor).

sentence.da: Hun er **kendt**, og alle i landet kender hende.
sentence.en: She is famous, and everyone in the country knows her.

ketchup.explanation: "Ketchup" means "ketchup". You do not count it, so you say noget ketchup (some ketchup).

sentence.da: Vil du have **ketchup** til pommes frites?
sentence.en: Do you want ketchup with the fries?

kikærter.explanation: "Kikærter" means "chickpeas", round beige beans often cooked in curries or added to salads. One chickpea is en kikært.

sentence.da: Hummus er lavet af **kikærter**, olie og hvidløg.
sentence.en: Hummus is made of chickpeas, oil and garlic.

kina.explanation: "Kina" means "China". Compare Jeg bor i Kina (I live in China) with Jeg rejser til Kina (I am traveling to China).

sentence.da: **Kina** er et stort land i Asien.
sentence.en: China is a big country in Asia.

kinesisk.explanation: "Kinesisk" means "Chinese", for the language and for things from China, and it is written with a small letter. Kinesisk mad means "Chinese food", and "Jeg taler kinesisk" means "I speak Chinese".

sentence.da: I Kina taler man **kinesisk**.
sentence.en: In China, people speak Chinese.

klam.explanation: "Klam" means "clammy", cold and unpleasantly sticky, and also "gross" in everyday talk. About a person's behavior it means creepy: Han er så klam (He is so creepy).

sentence.da: Efter regnen var tøjet **klam** og koldt.
sentence.en: After the rain, the clothes were clammy and cold.

klar.explanation: "Klar" means "ready" or "clear". Er du klar? means "Are you ready?" and "Det er klart" means "Of course" or "That is clear". Do not mix it up with færdig (finished), which says something is done, not that you are ready.

sentence.da: Maden er **klar**, og vi kan spise.
sentence.en: The food is ready, and we can eat.

klassisk.explanation: "Klassisk" means both "classical" and "classic", for something old that has lasted: en klassisk bil (a classic car). Its opposite is moderne (modern): moderne kunst (modern art).

sentence.da: Mozart og Beethoven skrev **klassisk** musik.
sentence.en: Mozart and Beethoven wrote classical music.

klatring.explanation: "En klatring" means "climbing", the sport of going up walls, rocks and mountains with your hands and feet. With en it can also be one single ascent.

forms.en: I do climbing as a sport.

sentence.da: Til **klatring** bruger man reb, sele og klatresko.
sentence.en: For climbing you use a rope, a harness and climbing shoes.

klimaforandring.explanation: "En klimaforandring" means "a climate change", a lasting shift in the weather of a region or of the whole Earth. When people talk about the global problem, they mostly use the plural: klimaforandringer (climate changes).

sentence.da: Den globale **klimaforandring** får havene til at stige.
sentence.en: The global climate change makes the oceans rise.

klimapolitik.explanation: "En klimapolitik" means "a climate policy", the laws and plans a government or party uses to cut emissions and slow global warming. A party can have its own: partiets klimapolitik (the party's climate policy).

sentence.da: Regeringens **klimapolitik** skal sænke Danmarks udledning af drivhusgasser.
sentence.en: The government's climate policy must lower Denmark's emissions of greenhouse gases.

klodset.explanation: "Klodset" means "clumsy", for someone who moves in a heavy, unskilled way and drops things. It also describes words or actions that come out badly: en klodset undskyldning (a clumsy apology).

sentence.da: Han taber ofte koppen, fordi han er så **klodset**.
sentence.en: He often drops the cup because he is so clumsy.

klog.explanation: "Klog" means "smart" and "wise", for people who think well. Det var ikke særlig klogt (That was not very smart) is a polite way to say something was a mistake.

sentence.da: Hun er meget **klog** for sin alder.
sentence.en: She is very smart for her age.

klokken.explanation: "Klokken" means "o'clock" and literally "the clock". Klokken er tre means "It is three o'clock", and you also use it for when something happens: Vi mødes klokken otte (We meet at eight o'clock). In writing, it is shortened to kl.

sentence.da: **Klokken** er otte om morgenen.
sentence.en: It is eight o'clock in the morning.

klokken er fem.explanation: "Klokken er fem" means "it is five o'clock". To give the time on the hour, say klokken er and the number. When you answer Hvad er klokken? (What time is it?) briefly, Danes often leave out klokken er and just say fem.

sentence.da: **Klokken er fem** nu.
sentence.en: It's five o'clock now.

knapt.explanation: "Knapt" means "barely" or "scarcely", and says that something is only just true or almost not true. With nok it gets stronger: Han har knapt nok sovet (He has hardly slept at all).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **knapt** høre dig, for musikken er for høj.
sentence.en: I can barely hear you because the music is too loud.

knust.explanation: "Knust" means "crushed", for things and for people: Glasset var knust (The glass was smashed). For a person it means "heartbroken": Hun er knust efter nyheden (She is heartbroken after the news).

sentence.da: Hun var **knust**, da han forlod hende.
sentence.en: She was heartbroken when he left her.

knækbrød.explanation: "Et knækbrød" means "a crispbread", a thin, dry, crunchy bread baked flat. The name comes from at knække (to snap), because it snaps when you break it.

sentence.da: Man kan smøre smør og ost på et **knækbrød**.
sentence.en: You can spread butter and cheese on a crispbread.

kobber.explanation: "Kobber" means "copper", the reddish-brown metal. It carries electricity and heat well, so it is also used for water pipes and cooking pots.

sentence.da: Elektriske ledninger er ofte lavet af **kobber**.
sentence.en: Electric wires are often made of copper.

kogt.explanation: "Kogt" means "boiled". Compare stegt (fried): en kogt kartoffel (a boiled potato) is cooked in water, but en stegt kartoffel (a fried potato) is cooked in a pan.

sentence.da: Kartoflen er **kogt** i varmt vand.
sentence.en: The potato is boiled in hot water.

kokain.explanation: "Kokain" means "cocaine", a strong, illegal narcotic. You mostly meet the word in news and crime reports: Politiet fandt kokain (The police found cocaine).

sentence.da: Det er ulovligt at købe og sælge **kokain**.
sentence.en: It is illegal to buy and sell cocaine.

kold.explanation: "Kold" means "cold", for weather, drinks and food, and also for people who seem unfriendly. To say you feel cold, use Jeg fryser (I am freezing), not Jeg er kold, which sounds as though you are an unfriendly person.

sentence.da: Det er en **kold** dag, og jeg fryser.
sentence.en: It is a cold day, and I am freezing.

kolesterol.explanation: "Kolesterol" means "cholesterol", a waxy substance in the body. Doctors check it because too much can narrow the arteries.

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at for højt **kolesterol** kan skade hjertet.
sentence.en: The doctor says that too high cholesterol can harm the heart.

kom nu.explanation: "Kom nu" means "come on", and literally "come now". It can encourage someone, as in Kom nu, du kan godt! (Come on, you can do it!). It can also push someone to go faster: Kom nu, vi skal af sted! (Come on, we have to go!). With a doubtful tone it shows you don't believe something: Kom nu, det passer ikke! (Come on, that is not true!).

forms.da: Kom nu, vi skal af sted.
forms.en: Come on, we have to go.

sentence.da: **Kom nu**, bussen kører snart!
sentence.en: Come on, the bus leaves soon!

kommende.explanation: "Kommende" means "upcoming" or "future", about something that will come: den kommende weekend (the coming weekend). It also fits a future role: mine kommende kolleger (my future colleagues).

sentence.da: Vi har et **kommende** møde på mandag.
sentence.en: We have an upcoming meeting on Monday.

kommunikation.explanation: "En kommunikation" means "communication", how people share thoughts and news with each other in speech, writing or media. It is often used for how well people understand each other at work or at home: Vi har brug for bedre kommunikation (We need better communication).

sentence.da: God **kommunikation** i teamet gør arbejdet lettere for alle.
sentence.en: Good communication in the team makes work easier for everyone.

kompetent.explanation: "Kompetent" means "competent", for someone who has the ability and knowledge to do a task well. It also fits what such a person gives: kompetent hjælp (competent help).

sentence.da: Lægen er meget **kompetent** og forklarer tingene godt.
sentence.en: The doctor is very competent and explains things well.

kompleks.explanation: "Kompleks" means "complex", something with many connected parts that is hard to understand fully. The everyday word for something hard to do is kompliceret (complicated); kompleks sounds more like science or a system with many parts.

sentence.da: Sagen er **kompleks**, fordi mange mennesker er involveret.
sentence.en: The case is complex because many people are involved.

komplet.explanation: "Komplet" means "complete", with all the parts. It also adds force: komplet umuligt (completely impossible).

sentence.da: Vi har nu et **komplet** sæt tallerkener.
sentence.en: We now have a complete set of plates.

kompliceret.explanation: "Kompliceret" means "complicated". It is the opposite of enkel (simple).

sentence.da: Det er en **kompliceret** situation, og ingen forstår den.
sentence.en: It is a complicated situation, and no one understands it.

kompost.explanation: "En kompost" means "a compost", rotted food scraps, leaves and cuttings that turn into rich soil for plants. It is also the bin or heap where this happens: Madaffald kommer i komposten (Food scraps go in the compost).

sentence.da: Kartoffelskræller og blade kan blive til **kompost** i haven.
sentence.en: Potato peels and leaves can turn into compost in the garden.

koncentreret.explanation: "Koncentreret" means "focused", for a person who gives full attention to something, and "concentrated", for a liquid that is strong because there is little water in it. To say that you focus, use at koncentrere sig: Jeg koncentrerer mig (I am concentrating).

sentence.da: Han sidder **koncentreret** og læser hele eftermiddagen.
sentence.en: He sits focused and reads all afternoon.

kondition.explanation: "En kondition" means "fitness", how long you can run, swim or bike before you are out of breath. Do not use it for the general state of something, as English "condition" can: for that Danes say tilstand.

sentence.da: Jeg løber hver dag for at få bedre **kondition**.
sentence.en: I run every day to get better fitness.

konfetti.explanation: "Konfetti" means "confetti", small colorful pieces of paper thrown to celebrate. It stays the same for one or many.

sentence.da: Bruden og gommen fik **konfetti** over hovedet.
sentence.en: The bride and groom got confetti over their heads.

kongelig.explanation: "Kongelig" means "royal", for what belongs to the monarch or the royal family. Many Danish institutions carry it in their name, for example Det Kongelige Teater (The Royal Theater).

sentence.da: Hun er **kongelig** og bor på Amalienborg i København.
sentence.en: She is royal and lives at Amalienborg in Copenhagen.

konkret.explanation: "Konkret" means "concrete" in the sense of clear and specific, not general: et konkret forslag (a specific proposal). It is not the building material, which is called beton.

sentence.da: Kan du give et **konkret** eksempel, så jeg forstår det?
sentence.en: Can you give a concrete example so that I understand it?

konkurs.explanation: "Konkurs" means "bankrupt" and "bankruptcy", when a firm cannot pay what it owes and has to close. The usual phrase is at gå konkurs (to go bankrupt): Firmaet gik konkurs (The company went bankrupt).

sentence.da: Butikken måtte lukke, fordi ejeren ikke kunne betale og var **konkurs**.
sentence.en: The shop had to close because the owner could not pay and was bankrupt.

konservativ.explanation: "Konservativ" means "conservative", for people or views that prefer to keep traditions and keep things as they are. In Denmark it is also the name of a party, Det Konservative Folkeparti.

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er meget **konservativ** og kan ikke lide forandringer.
sentence.en: My grandfather is very conservative and does not like changes.

konstant.explanation: "Konstant" means "constant", something that keeps going without change: Der er konstant larm (There is constant noise). It also works for something that stays the same: en konstant temperatur (a constant temperature).

sentence.da: Telefonen ringer **konstant**, og det stopper aldrig.
sentence.en: The phone rings constantly, and it never stops.

kontant.explanation: "Kontant" means "cash" or "in cash". Compare Jeg betaler kontant (I pay in cash) with Jeg betaler med kort (I pay by card). A sign saying Kun kontant means "Cash only".

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke kort og betaler **kontant**.
sentence.en: I have no card and pay in cash.

kontanthjælp.explanation: "En kontanthjælp" means "a welfare benefit", money from the municipality (kommunen) to adults who have no work or other income. It is built from kontant (cash) and hjælp (help).

sentence.da: Hun får **kontanthjælp**, når hun hverken har job eller penge.
sentence.en: She gets welfare when she has neither a job nor money.

korrekt.explanation: "Korrekt" means "correct", and sounds a bit formal: Svaret er korrekt (The answer is correct). In everyday talk, people often say rigtig (right) instead.

sentence.da: Du får point, fordi dit svar er **korrekt**.
sentence.en: You get points because your answer is correct.

korrupt.explanation: "Korrupt" means "corrupt", for people or systems that misuse power for personal gain. The matching word for the thing itself is korruption (corruption).

sentence.da: Dommeren tog imod penge og var derfor **korrupt**.
sentence.en: The judge accepted money and was therefore corrupt.

kort.explanation: "Kort" means "short", for length and for time. There is also a different word et kort, which means "a card" or "a map".

sentence.da: Hans hår er **kort**, ikke langt.
sentence.en: His hair is short, not long.

kort sagt.explanation: "Kort sagt" means "in short" and comes before the main point of what you have been saying. It is built from kort (short) and sagt (said).

sentence.da: **Kort sagt**, jeg kan ikke komme i morgen.
sentence.en: In short, I cannot come tomorrow.

kortvarig.explanation: "Kortvarig" means "short-lived", for an effect, a visit or a feeling that is over quickly.

sentence.da: Smerten var **kortvarig**, og efter en time var den væk.
sentence.en: The pain was short-lived, and after an hour it was gone.

kostbar.explanation: "Kostbar" means "costly" or "precious", for something worth a lot. It can be about money, but it also fits what matters to you: kostbare minder (precious memories).

sentence.da: Vi må ikke spilde tiden, fordi den er **kostbar**.
sentence.en: We must not waste time because it is precious.

kraftig.explanation: "Kraftig" means "strong" in the sense of powerful or heavy, for wind, rain, blows and sounds. About a person's body it means heavily built, so for muscles and strength Danes say stærk instead.

sentence.da: Der var **kraftig** regn hele natten, så gaden stod under vand.
sentence.en: There was heavy rain all night, so the street was flooded.

kraftigt.explanation: "Kraftigt" means "strongly" or "heavily", and tells how hard or how much something happens. In the news it often goes with change: Valutaen faldt kraftigt (The currency fell sharply).

sentence.da: Priserne steg **kraftigt**, og mange har svært ved at betale.
sentence.en: Prices rose sharply, and many have trouble paying.

kreativ.explanation: "Kreativ" means "creative" and describes a person or an idea that is new and different. It fits things too: en kreativ løsning (a creative solution).

sentence.da: Hun er **kreativ** og tegner mange flotte billeder.
sentence.en: She is creative and draws many nice pictures.

kreativitet.explanation: "En kreativitet" means "creativity", the ability to think up new ideas or make something original. It is used for art, but also for solving problems at work: Vi har brug for kreativitet i løsningen (We need creativity in the solution).

sentence.da: Børn har masser af **kreativitet**, når de tegner og leger.
sentence.en: Children have lots of creativity when they draw and play.

kredit.explanation: "En kredit" means "credit", the right to take goods or money now and pay for them later. A shop or a bank can give it to you.

sentence.da: Hun købte sofaen på **kredit** og betaler hver måned.
sentence.en: She bought the sofa on credit and pays every month.

kriminalitet.explanation: "Kriminalitet" means "crime" in general, not one single act. One single crime is en forbrydelse (a crime).

sentence.da: Der er meget lidt **kriminalitet** i vores lille by.
sentence.en: There is very little crime in our small town.

kriminel.explanation: "Kriminel" means "criminal", about crime or breaking the law: kriminel adfærd (criminal behavior). On its own, en kriminel (a criminal) is a person who breaks the law.

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en **kriminel** bande i byen.
sentence.en: The police found a criminal gang in the city.

kristen.explanation: "Kristen" means "Christian", about the faith that follows Jesus Christ, and it is written with a small letter. A Christian person is en kristen.

sentence.da: Hun er **kristen** og går i kirke hver søndag.
sentence.en: She is Christian and goes to church every Sunday.

kristendom.explanation: "Kristendom" means "Christianity", the religion based on the life and teaching of Jesus. Many Danes belong to the national church, which is called folkekirken.

sentence.da: **Kristendom** er den største religion i Danmark.
sentence.en: Christianity is the biggest religion in Denmark.

kritik.explanation: "Kritik" means "criticism". To give it, say at komme med kritik (to offer criticism).

forms.en: He got a lot of criticism.

sentence.da: Hun fik meget **kritik** for sin tale.
sentence.en: She got a lot of criticism for her speech.

kritisk.explanation: "Kritisk" means "critical" in two ways: judging carefully and asking questions, as in kritisk tænkning (critical thinking), and serious or dangerous, as in en kritisk situation (a critical situation).

sentence.da: Man skal være **kritisk**, når man læser nyheder på nettet.
sentence.en: You should be critical when you read news online.

krudt.explanation: "Et krudt" means "gunpowder", the explosive powder that was used in old guns and cannons. In the saying Han har ikke opfundet krudtet (He did not invent gunpowder), it means someone is not very clever.

sentence.da: Fyrværkeri indeholder **krudt**, og det brænder meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: Fireworks contain gunpowder, and it burns very fast.

krydderier.explanation: "Krydderier" means "spices", the dry things that add taste to food. Fresh green ones are urter (herbs).

sentence.da: Kanel og karry er **krydderier**.
sentence.en: Cinnamon and curry are spices.

krydret.explanation: "Krydret" means "spicy" or "seasoned", with lots of flavor from herbs and spices. Burning hot like chili is stærk (hot): Den er for stærk (It is too hot).

sentence.da: Karry og peber gør maden **krydret**.
sentence.en: Curry and pepper make the food spicy.

kræft.explanation: "Kræft" means "cancer", the illness where body cells grow out of control. To name the kind, put the body part in front: hudkræft (skin cancer).

sentence.da: Hun havde **kræft**, men blev rask efter behandlingen.
sentence.en: She had cancer but got well after the treatment.

krøllet.explanation: "Krøllet" means "curly" for hair, and "wrinkled" for cloth or paper that is not smooth. Which meaning fits depends on the thing it describes.

sentence.da: Min lillesøster har **krøllet** hår, mens jeg har lige hår.
sentence.en: My little sister has curly hair, while I have straight hair.

kul.explanation: "Kul" means "coal", the black rock that is dug out of the ground and burned for heat and electricity. Charcoal for the grill is called trækul.

sentence.da: Før i tiden fyrede man i ovnen med **kul** for at få varme.
sentence.en: In the past people fired the stove with coal to get warmth.

kulde.explanation: "Kulde" means "cold", the low temperature itself. Do not mix it up with kold (cold), which describes something: koldt vand (cold water).

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der sne og **kulde**.
sentence.en: In winter there is snow and cold.

kulhydrat.explanation: "Et kulhydrat" means "a carbohydrate", the part of food such as bread, pasta, rice and potatoes that gives the body energy.

sentence.da: Der er meget **kulhydrat** i pasta og ris.
sentence.en: There is a lot of carbohydrate in pasta and rice.

kulstof.explanation: "Kulstof" means "carbon", the chemical element that all living things contain. It is built from kul (coal) and stof (substance), so literally "coal stuff".

sentence.da: Planter og dyr består blandt andet af **kulstof**.
sentence.en: Plants and animals consist partly of carbon.

kun.explanation: "Kun" means "only" or "just", and it limits the word that comes after it. Kun jeg ved det means "Only I know it", while Jeg ved kun det means "That is all I know".
